title: feat(post): keep the .mch part tree as MachineTree
body:
## What changed

- `camcraft_post::machine` has a new pure data type, `MachineTree`, and a new reader, `parse_mch_tree` (new file `crates/post/src/machine/tree.rs`).
- The reader keeps each part of `kinematics.default.parts`: its `id`, `name`, `type`, the index of its parent, and the facts that the file states (`travel`, `axis`, `pivot`, `offset`, `direction`, the spindle body, the tool station).
- All lengths are in mm. The reader uses the unit factor of `parse_mch`. An angle is not scaled.
- Each linear and rotary part has a moving side. An axis that is an ancestor of a `head` part moves the tool. Each other axis moves the table. A tree with no head states no side.
- A malformed tree refuses. The message names the part id and the key.
- `Machine`, `parse_mch` and the existing checks do not change.
- `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` has a short note about the new reader.

## Cause

`collect_axes` in `parse.rs` flattens the part tree into `Machine.axes`. The parent chain is lost. A machine model (#2574) needs the chain.

## Tests

New suite `crates/post/tests/machine_tree.rs` (8 tests):

- `every_shipped_machine_file_reads_as_a_tree`: each of the 45 `assets/machines/*.mch` files parses. The tree and `parse_mch` state the same number of axes.
- `the_three_axis_vmc_keeps_its_parent_chain` (`vmc.mch`)
- `the_tilt_head_puts_the_head_chain_on_the_tool_side` (`tilthead.mch`)
- `an_inch_file_scales_lengths_and_keeps_angles` (`tormach-770mx-microarc4.mch`)
- `a_hand_written_inch_tree_scales_each_length_and_no_angle`
- `the_mirror_form_default_machine_states_no_part_tree` (`3axis-vmc.mch`)
- `a_tree_with_no_head_states_no_moving_side`
- `a_malformed_tree_refuses_by_part_id_and_key` (17 malformed trees)

Mutation results:

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| `mod.rs` as on `upstream/main` (no `tree` module) | red: the suite does not compile (`unresolved imports ... parse_mch_tree`) |
| No unit factor on `travel` | red: 2 tests fail |
| Moving side swapped | red: 4 tests fail |
| Duplicate `id` guard off | red: `a_malformed_tree_refuses_by_part_id_and_key` |
| Unknown `type` accepted | red: `a_malformed_tree_refuses_by_part_id_and_key` |
| Fix restored | green: 8 passed |

The suite was written before the reader. Its first run on unchanged code did not finish (the build was stopped at a time limit). The first mutation above is the proof that it is red without the change.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green (71 steps, 0 failed, on base `3e615d653`). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Goldens moved

None. No `.nc` or `.cl` file changed.

## Not exercised

- No code uses `MachineTree` yet. The simulator work of #2574 is the first user.
- `3axis-vmc.mch` is written in the mirror form (`kinematics.static`). It states no part tree, so it reads as an empty tree. The 3-axis parent chain is pinned on `vmc.mch`.
- Most shipped 3-axis files put the `head` beside the axis chain (`base > col > ram > sld` and `base > head`). By the rule of the issue, all their axes read as table side. Only `tilthead.mch`, `sinker-edm.mch` and `millturn.mch` state a tool-side axis. A correct model needs those machine files nested as the machine moves. This PR does not change a machine file. See `docs/decisions/2583-machine-tree.md`.
- The tree door also refuses `zero_offset`, `rollover` and `sign_convention` on a part that is not a rotary, because it uses `trunnion::parse_axis_fields`. No shipped file states them there.

## Overlaps

- #2554 touches `crates/post/src/machine/mod.rs` and `parse.rs`: the same files, different lines and functions. This PR adds two module lines in `mod.rs` and makes `rate`, `mm_factor` and `scale` `pub(super)` in `parse.rs`. Whichever merges second refreshes.

The type is `feat`: the issue is an enhancement (`P4`), so this PR merges at the next cut.

Changelog: Post: the `.mch` part tree is kept as `MachineTree` (`parse_mch_tree`), with the parent chain and the moving side of each axis, for the machine model (#2583).

Effort: medium

Fixes #2583

title: perf(3d): facet grid for the drop-cutter support scan
body:
## What changed

- The support facets of 3D finishing are now a `SupSet` (`crates/motion/src/finishing3d/grid.rs`). A `SupSet` holds the facets and a uniform XY bucket grid in CSR layout (Ericson, "Real-Time Collision Detection", ch. 7).
- These point scans read only the facets of the cell that holds the query point:
  - `support_at`
  - `support_grad`
  - `ball_clear`
  - `column_clear`
  - `edge::fold_best`
- Each scan keeps its own padded-box reject. Each cell lists its facets in ascending index, one time each. Thus the same f64 code runs on the same facets in the same order, and each answer has the same bits as the full scan.
- The cell map is monotone. A facet whose padded box holds the point is always in the cell of the point.
- The grid falls back to the full scan for a non-finite box, a non-finite query point, an extent that is not finite, more than `u32::MAX` facets, or an extent that no cell size fits. It never guesses a cell.
- `SupSet::full_scan` keeps the old scan as the reference. The GPU filter of #2526 can compare against it.
- Each `&[Sup]` parameter in `finishing3d` is now `&SupSet`. The loops that are not point queries read every facet, as before.
- Decision entry: `docs/decisions/2619-facet-grid.md`.

## Readings

Release build, parallel finishing, a height-field mesh, tool diameter 6, tolerance 0.01. One run each, with a temporary harness that is not committed.

| Facets | Before | After | Output hash (before = after) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1800 | 13.161 s | 13.908 s | `a629dd9f259d227d` |
| 7200 | 162.915 s | 161.515 s | `c719175f144437ae` |

The grid gives no measurable gain on this job. The point scans are not the hot path here. The output is the same. A profile must find the hot path before more speed work.

## Pinning tests

Lib unit tests in `crates/motion/src/finishing3d/grid_tests.rs`. The scan functions are `pub(super)`, so a file in `crates/motion/tests/` cannot reach them.

- `grid_scan_matches_full_scan_on_bumps`: tool radius 0.4, 0.5, 1 and 3 against cell 1, 0.37, 5 and the automatic size. Boxes on cell borders, and a tool larger than a cell.
- `grid_scan_matches_full_scan_on_big_and_degenerate_facets`: facets larger than many cells, a steep wall, zero-area facets (one point, a repeated vertex, a collinear facet).
- `grid_candidates_hold_every_facet_whose_box_holds_the_point`: the superset law, the order and no duplicates.
- `non_finite_input_falls_back_to_the_full_scan`: NaN and infinite vertices, non-finite query points, an empty set.

The parity tests compare the bits of `support_at`, `support_grad`, `fold_best`, `plunge_support`, `ball_clear` and `column_clear` between the grid and the full scan. A test mutation (a miss of 2% of a cell at the upper edge) makes two tests fail.

Quick gate on `2eefe69e5d6796e3bbfd35b4be5130b7dc7b767c`: 27 steps, 0 failed (motion lib and the finish3d suites, app `golden_cl` and `operations` included). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean. No golden `.cl` or `.nc` file changed.

## Not exercised

- The release lanes and the large-fixture golden runs (`#[ignore]`).
- Parallel raster lines (the optional item of the issue). Not done.
- The speed on the real part models. The readings come from one synthetic mesh.

Changelog: 3D finishing: the drop-cutter support scan uses a facet grid; the toolpaths do not change.

Effort: high

Fixes #2619

title: feat(sim): f32 twin of the cell cut kernel and the brick work list
body:
## What changed

GPU stock sim S1 (#2626). This PR adds a CPU f32 twin of the per-cell cut kernel and the brick work list. The change is additive. No caller changes, and the f64 kernel does not change.

- `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/cut_twin.rs`: the f32 cell cut.
  - Coordinates are relative to the tile. The tile is the brick (8 cells a side).
  - The ball uses the capsule closed form. The upright flat uses the level closed form, the plunge closed form, or a 32-step golden section. This is the same order as `Sweep::dist` in f64.
  - The kernel adds a margin to each distance before it claims a cell: `TWIN_ULPS` (32) f32 epsilons of the tile scale, plus `1e-6` of the path length on the flat path. Thus the twin never removes more than the f64 cut.
  - `ordered_bits` / `from_ordered_bits` give the order-preserving u32 key. The max law runs on that key, which is the law of a GPU `atomicMax`.
- `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/cut_twin_work.rs`: the brick work list and its CPU run.
  - The window of each chord is the f64 `Sweep::window`, clipped to the `pack_cut` lattice. The items are sorted by brick, then by chord.
  - `run_twin` writes the cut layer in the dense layout of `preview::pack_cut`, with the same `-4 cap` floor.
  - The twin refuses by name: each tool other than the ball and the flat end mill, an arc, a tilted axis, a zero-length move, a non-finite value, a bad tool size, and a chord window above `TWIN_MAX_CELLS_PER_CHORD`.
- `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/mod.rs`: the two modules and their exports.
- `docs/decisions/2626-f32-cut-twin.md`: 8 decisions taken unattended.

## Readings

- One-sided parity on a 16 x 16 x 8 block (cell 0.7, cap 2.8), with a level feed, a ramp, a plunge, a diagonal ramp and a rapid.
  - `twin <= f64` holds with no tolerance for each texel. The f64-to-f32 pack rounding keeps order.
  - `twin >= f64 - tol`, with `tol = 96 * eps * 64 + 1e-4` (about 7.3e-4 mm). The test comment gives the reason for the bound.
- The two values clamp at `-cap` before the compare. A cut below `-cap` never shows.

## Pinning tests

`crates/sim/tests/stock_cut_twin.rs`:
- `the_ball_twin_never_removes_more_than_the_f64_cut`
- `the_flat_twin_never_removes_more_than_the_f64_cut`
- `the_ordered_key_keeps_the_order_of_negative_zero_and_positive`
- `the_batch_answers_bit_for_bit_in_any_move_order`
- `the_work_list_covers_every_claimed_cell_inside_its_bricks`
- `degenerate_input_refuses_with_a_clean_error`
- `every_other_tool_refuses_by_name`

Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`) on head 65e391e04: 78 steps, 0 failed, not VOID. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised

- GPU and WGSL code. That is S2.
- Arc moves, tilted poses and the other tools. The twin refuses them.
- The ray-entry layers (`cut_ups`, `cut_downs`).
- Lattices larger than the test fixture, and large world offsets.

## Changelog

Changelog: Stock simulation: an f32 CPU reference of the GPU cell cut and its brick work list (no user-visible change yet).

Effort: high

Fixes #2626

title: refactor(app): tool-number follow-ups of #2488
body:
## What changed

The four follow-up items of the second review of PR #2488 (#2517).

1. **Two long files are split.**
   - `crates/app/src/commands/tool_import.rs` (401 lines): `ImportMode` and `ImportReport` (the mode an import runs under and the report its status line reads) move to the new `commands/tool_import_report.rs` (97 lines). `tool_import` re-exports them, so `commands::{ImportMode, ImportReport}` and `commands::tool_import::*` do not change. `tool_import.rs` is now 312 lines. The gate map of `tool_import_modes.rs` names the new module.
   - `crates/app/tests/tool_numbers.rs` (476 lines): the tests of numbers that never shift (#2442) and of legacy loads move to `tests/tool_numbers/stable.rs` (`#[path]` module, the pattern of `keep_law.rs`). Sizes now: 354 and 247 lines. The `#[test]` count of the binary goes from 10 to 13 (no test removed).
2. **Two legacy-load tests** (in `stable.rs`):
   - `a_legacy_project_numbers_by_name_order_not_by_document_order`: a pre-#2442 file whose entity order is not the name order. A save always writes name order, so the test moves `EM-0600-4FL` to the front of the entity list by hand (as an older build or an edit leaves a file). The load gives `EM-0400-2FL` T1 and `EM-0600-4FL` T2, and the post writes `T01` / `T02`.
   - `a_legacy_project_mixing_numbered_and_unnumbered_tools_keeps_both`: `EM-0400-2FL` carries T7, `AA-SPARE` and `EM-0600-4FL` carry no number. The load keeps T7 and gives each other tool its place in the name-sorted list of all tools: `AA-SPARE` 1, `EM-0600-4FL` 3. The posted numbers then hold when a tool is added and when one is deleted.
3. **No `u32::MAX` fallback.** The new `tool_numbers::assign` gives each unnumbered tool the lowest free number in order, and refuses by name when none of 1-99999 is free: `tool 'X' has no tool number and none of 1-99999 is free - give it its own tool number`. `tool_numbers::numbers` now returns `Result`:
   - the post (`posting::op_streams_by`) and `ImportTools` propagate the refusal;
   - `clash` (the tool list page and the post's clash law) returns it as the refusal;
   - `number_of` and `next_free` read it as `None` (the tool list export shows `?`; `next_free` is correct, because then no number is free).
4. **No dead branch.** `SetToolNumber` keeps its number as a `u32` (`new` already refuses `None`, #2442) and has `number()`, as `AddTool` has. `crates/ui/src/state.rs` writes `tool <name> is now T<n>` from it, and the `None => "number cleared"` arm is gone.

The comment over the T/H law in `posting.rs` said "else its 1-based position among the named tools in document order". That is not true since #2442. It now says what the code does.

## Tests

Pinned by (`camcraft-app`, `--test tool_numbers`):
- `an_unnumbered_tool_with_no_free_number_is_refused_by_name` (`assign` with 99999 numbered tools and one without; then the lowest-free case).
- `stable::a_legacy_project_numbers_by_name_order_not_by_document_order`.
- `stable::a_legacy_project_mixing_numbered_and_unnumbered_tools_keeps_both`.

`cargo test -p camcraft-app --test tool_numbers`: 13 passed. With the name sort in `freeze_legacy_tool_numbers` removed, the name-order test fails (`first by name: left Some(2), right Some(1)`).

Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`, Linux, 12 cores, another build running on the box): 384 steps, 383 ok, 1 failed.
- `app suites: tool_numbers`: 13 passed. `app suites: tool_import_modes`: 9 passed.
- `ui suites: lib`: 1203 passed, 0 failed.
- The other app and ui suites that the gate selected: ok.
- `app suites: continuous_4axis_part`: FAIL, but not from this change. `examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.camproj` on `upstream/main` (1ae4d061f) is project version 70, and `PROJECT_VERSION` is 71: `... is stale; regenerate with WRITE_GOLDEN=1: /version: 71 != 70`. This PR does not touch the project format or that example.

`cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean in the files of this PR. One error is on `upstream/main` too: `clippy::drop_non_drop` at `crates/app/tests/import_step_thread.rs:133` (from d7bbf723a). With `-A clippy::drop_non_drop` the run is clean.

The branch merges cleanly with `upstream/main` (`git merge-tree`).

- No run in the app. The UI status text for a number change is the same as before (`tool <name> is now T<n>`, pinned by `setting_a_tool_number_is_a_command_with_undo`).
- The refusal of item 3 is reached only by a fixture or a hand-made document with 99999 numbered tools. The test calls `assign` directly; it does not build 99999 tool entities.

title: test(app): pin the gouge refusal of each tilted operation kind
body:
## What changed

This PR adds tests only. The new binary `crates/app/tests/tilted_gouge_kinds.rs` audits each operation kind that accepts a tilt.

- Each probe cuts into a correct box part (a synthetic mesh with 12 facets) in a box stock on the 4th-axis mill (`tormach-770mx-microarc4.mch`).
- Each probe runs at A 90 and at A -90. Each probe also runs upright as a guard, except 2D Adaptive. Each pose has its own world.
- The test asserts three things:
  - a blocking verdict at generation (`Warning::Gouge`, or `Warning::StockChamferGouge` for the 2D Chamfer);
  - a refused post (`post blocked`, and `cuts past the finish surface` when the op is tilted);
  - no file is written.

The decision entry is `docs/decisions/2720-tilted-gouge-audit.md`.

## Results

| Kind | Probe | Test | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Face | stock source, cut 1 mm under the part skin | `a_tilted_face_into_the_part_is_refused` | refused |
| Contour | whole part, Outside, a second part 2 mm past the wall along X | `a_tilted_contour_into_a_neighbour_part_is_refused` | refused |
| Pocket | whole part, area offset 3 mm into the part | `a_tilted_pocket_offset_into_the_part_is_refused` | refused |
| 2D Adaptive | whole part, area offset 3 mm into the part | `a_tilted_adaptive_offset_into_the_part_is_refused` (A 90), `a_tilted_adaptive_offset_into_the_part_is_refused_at_a_minus_90` | refused |
| 2D Offset | whole part, area offset 3 mm into the part | `a_tilted_offset2d_offset_into_the_part_is_refused` | refused |
| Engrave | whole part, 7 mm deep on a 3 mm mark budget | `a_tilted_engrave_deeper_than_a_mark_is_refused` | refused |
| Trace | whole part, 7 mm deep on a 3 mm mark budget | `a_tilted_trace_deeper_than_a_mark_is_refused` | refused |
| 2D Chamfer | stock source, the part fills the stock | `a_tilted_chamfer_of_the_stock_into_the_part_is_refused` | refused (`StockChamferGouge`) |
| Circular | stock source, cut 1 mm under the part skin | `a_tilted_circular_into_the_part_is_refused` | refused |
| Slot | - | `tilted_gouge.rs` (#2600), not repeated | refused |

No kind posts a tilted gouge, so this PR files no P1.

## Where a tilted gouge cannot be expressed

- **Contour into its own part:** the app refuses this at create. Side Inside on a whole section is refused ("needs picked rings"). A negative stock to leave is refused ("not usable"). Thus the probe uses a neighbour part. The gap is along X, the tilt axis, so the neighbour stays beside the wall in each pose.
- **2D Chamfer on a part source:** this has no depth law by design, because the chamfer must break the part edge. Thus only the stock-source chamfer (#1631) can express a gouge.

## Readings

- Quick gate `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` on 678f3a37e: 1 step, 0 failed. `app suites: tilted_gouge_kinds` is ok in 52 s (10 passed, 0 ignored).

## Not exercised

- B rotation, compound A+B tilts, and `basis_version` 0. All probes use `basis_version` 1, B 0, A 90 or -90.
- Tilts that are not a quarter turn (for example A 30).
- Upright 2D Adaptive: in debug it takes more than 60 s, and the keep law suite (#1603) covers it.
- Picked-ring (Selection) sources. All probes use the whole part or the stock.
- TrochoidalSlot, Probe and PlasmaProfile: they have no tilt.
- Observation: a 2D Adaptive with `optimal_load` 0.5 on this fixture ran for more than 9 minutes in debug. I stopped it. I did not measure it in release. Filed as #2736.

The stale comments near `params.rs:1365` and `sane.rs:112` are not in touched lines, so this PR does not change them.

title: fix(import): log a curved STEP face the fit cannot measure, mark reduced fidelity
body:
Stacked on #2731. Merge #2731 first (retarget order: AGENTS.md "Overlapping issues stack"). Until then, the diff against `main` also shows the #2731 commits.

## What changed

- `step_fit.rs`: `fit()` returns `Result<Fit, &'static str>`. Each silent `return KEPT` of the parameter check is now an `Err` with a reason:
  - no surface parameters;
  - parameters that do not give the mesh's points;
  - a facet that is not a triangle;
  - a point index that the mesh does not hold;
  - more points than the fit can count;
  - a pass tolerance that is not positive;
  - no surface in the shell (in `fit_face`).
- A new `judged(index, fit)` takes the result for face `index`. On `Err` it logs `step: face <n> keeps the kernel's facets unmeasured (<reason>); the model is reduced fidelity` and reports the face as `UNMEASURED` (1000 file units). The model is then reduced fidelity (#864) and verify refuses.
- `fit_face` takes the face index. `step.rs` passes it on the same line (the file stays at 400 lines).
- Decision entry: `docs/decisions/2719-step-fit-fallback-diagnostic.md` (mark, not measure; why).

## Readings

- Fallback, no parameters (face index 3): log `step: face 4 keeps the kernel's facets unmeasured (its mesh carries no surface parameters); the model is reduced fidelity`. Reported height: before 0 (full fidelity, no log); after 1000 file units.
- Fallback, parameters 0.1 mm off the points (face index 0): log `step: face 1 keeps the kernel's facets unmeasured (its mesh's parameters do not give its points); the model is reduced fidelity`. Reported height: before 0; after 1000 file units.
- Bar fixture `bar_cross_holes.step`: 0.005 mm before and after (no fallback on it). No STEP fixture in the 22 quick-gate suites goes to reduced fidelity.

## Pinning tests

`crates/app/src/geometry/import/step_fit_tests.rs` (lib):
- `a_face_without_surface_parameters_is_logged_and_reported_unmeasured`
- `a_face_whose_parameters_miss_its_points_is_logged_and_reported_unmeasured`

Each captures the log, and asserts the face number and the reason in it. It asserts that the kernel's facets are kept and that the face reports `UNMEASURED`, also through `step_facets::facets_of`. It asserts that `step::coarse` gives reduced fidelity for each file unit from the micrometre to the kilometre, and that the value is never the unknown-fidelity sentinel.

Quick gate on head 1111b8402: 22 steps, 0 failed. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- No real STEP file from a different writer that causes the fallback. The pins use synthetic meshes.
- The refusal that the user sees is the general `TOO_COARSE` text ("re-import with a larger STEP facet budget"). A larger budget does not help an unmeasured face. Only the log names the true cause. Follow-up filed (see the issue comment).
- The kept mesh of an unmeasured face is not measured (the decision entry says why).
- `feature_edge_g1_join` (#2713) is not in the quick plan of this diff.

Changelog: STEP import logs a curved face whose facets it cannot measure, and marks the model reduced fidelity so that verify refuses, in place of a silent full-fidelity import.

Fixes #2719

title: fix(import): report the height of the kept curved STEP facets
body:
## What changed

- `step_fit.rs`: the curved-face fit (#2600) measures every edge of the facets that it keeps, inside and boundary. It reports the highest edge height times a bound for the inside of a facet:
  - cylinder: 1.0;
  - cone, sphere, torus: 1.5 (the two-way bound is 4/3, from Waldron, SIAM J. Numer. Anal. 35, 1998; 1.5 adds a margin).
- The import takes the larger of this value and the pass tolerance as the chord (`step.rs` was already `kept.tol.max(off)`; it is not changed).
- The split limit of an inside edge is now `tol / kind.inside()`. Before, it was `2 x tol`, and the import reported `tol`.
- `step_facets.rs`: one doc comment only.
- Decision entry: `docs/decisions/2718-step-chord-kept-height.md`.

## Readings

Bar fixture `bar_cross_holes.step` (chord that the import reports):

| | chord |
|---|---|
| before (main) | 0.005 mm, while the kept wall edges stood up to about 0.01 mm off |
| honest report, old `2 x tol` split | 0.00999 mm (over `CHORD_CAP` 0.005 mm: reduced fidelity) |
| after (this PR) | 0.005 mm |

Synthetic faces (unit pins, `TOL` 0.005 mm). The lattice boundary edges are not split, so they set the worst value. Before this PR the fit reported 0 for each face, and the import reported 0.005 mm.

| face | reported after | sampled worst of the kept facets |
|---|---|---|

title: fix(import): flip the flat cap facets of a refined STEP face
body:
## What changed

- `crates/app/src/geometry/import/step_fit.rs`: a new step `relax` runs after the split of #2600, on each face that the split changed. It flips an inside edge when the two angles opposite to it sum to more than a half turn (Lawson's edge flip, measured in space).
- A flip is made only when the two new facets keep their winding in the parameter plane, and the new edge passes the chord-height limit of the split. No point moves. No boundary edge changes. The facet count does not change.
- `crates/app/tests/tilted_gouge.rs`: one new test for the normals of the bar's wall facets.
- `docs/decisions/2713-step-cap-facets.md`: the decision and the dropped options.
- `crates/kernel/tests/step_agreement.rs`: the missing triage row for `bar_cross_holes.step` and its named pin.

The kernel refuses this fixture with `solidcore refuses: #655 at read: pcurves failed on`. The mesh reports `no exact solid to judge against`. The row records a named refusal, not import agreement.

## Cause

The join law (#2215) was not the cause. The cause is the STEP importer.

The split of #2600 measures facet edges only. On the wall of `bar_cross_holes.step` it left flat "cap" facets: three points on the cylinder, with the apex over the middle of the long edge. Each edge of such a facet is within the limit. The normal of the facet is not: it stood up to 65.5 degrees off the radius.

The feature graph uses a crease angle of 40 degrees. It read the edges of the cap facets as creases on the smooth wall, and some cap facets as faces of their own. These false edges were the 116 split pieces of the test.

## Readings (`bar_cross_holes.step`)

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| wall facets | 131 834 | 131 834 |
| wall facets with a normal more than 25 degrees off the radius | 2 147 | 0 |
| worst wall normal | 65.5 degrees | 6.5 degrees |

| split pieces | 116 | 0 |
| import time of the normals test (debug build) | 2.6 s | 5.5 s |

Pins:

- `tilted_gouge`: `the_step_bars_wall_facet_normals_follow_the_cylinder` (new). It pins the cause in the importer.
- `step_agreement`: `step_bar_cross_holes` pins the fixture triage. `step_files_agree_or_refuse_by_name` pins coverage of every STEP fixture. Both tests pass.

Mutation: with `step_fit.rs` of `upstream/main`, the two pins are red (116 split pieces; 2 147 facets, worst 65.5 degrees). With the fix, the two pins are green.

Kernel row mutation: removing the `bar_cross_holes.step` row makes `step_bar_cross_holes` and `step_files_agree_or_refuse_by_name` red. Restoring the row makes the suite green.

The review fix also passes the explicit suites: `camcraft-kernel --test step_agreement` (20 passed) and `camcraft-app --test feature_edge_g1_join` (5 passed).

- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-kernel --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

- The pins of #2600 stay green: `a_tilted_slot_into_the_step_bar_is_refused`, `the_step_bars_wall_facets_lie_on_the_cylinder`.

None. No `.nc` or `.cl` file changed.

title: feat(geometry): conservative bit-packed raster of geo2d regions
body:
## What changed

This PR adds `camcraft_geometry::nesting::raster`, slice 1 of the raster nest (#2525). The module is CPU code only. It has no GPU code, no new crate, no new crate edge and no new external dependency.

- `crates/geometry/src/nesting.rs`: the module root (provenance line).
- `crates/geometry/src/nesting/raster.rs`: `RasterGrid`, `BitRaster`, `RasterError`, the limits and the two public functions.
- `crates/geometry/src/nesting/raster/scan.rs`: the integer scan conversion.
- `crates/geometry/tests/nesting_raster.rs`: 10 tests.
- `docs/decisions/2612-nesting-raster.md`: the unattended decisions.

Public API:

```rust
pub const DEFAULT_CELL_UNITS: i64; // 1 mm
pub const MAX_CELLS: u64;          // 2^24 (4096 x 4096)
pub const MAX_SIDE: u32;           // 2^16
pub fn cell_units_from_mm(mm: f64) -> Result<i64, RasterError>;
RasterGrid::new(origin_x, origin_y, cell, width, height) -> Result<RasterGrid, RasterError>;
RasterGrid::covering(&Region, cell) -> Result<RasterGrid, RasterError>; // origin on the global lattice
pub fn rasterize_over(&Region, &RasterGrid) -> Result<BitRaster, RasterError>; // parts
pub fn rasterize_free(&Region, &RasterGrid) -> Result<BitRaster, RasterError>; // usable sheet
BitRaster::{grid, words, get, count_ones}
```

How it works:

1. The vertices are quantized with the `geo2d` bridge rule (1 unit = 1 um). After that, each cell decision uses exact `i128` arithmetic with checked multiply and add. No float takes part in a cell decision.
2. Pass "touched": each cell whose closed square touches a closed boundary edge. The x extent of an edge in a row slab is rounded outward, and a value on a cell line touches the two cells.
3. Pass "centre inside": even-odd parity of a +x ray at each cell centre, with the half-open edge rule of `geo2d`. Doubled coordinates keep the centre an integer.
4. Over = touched OR centre inside. Free = centre inside AND NOT touched.

A closed square that meets the region but no edge is fully in the interior, so its centre is inside. Thus "over" contains each point of the region. A square with no edge contact and an inside centre is fully in the interior. Thus a "free" cell is a true free cell. Holes are not free.

Rows are packed in `u32` words (LSB first). Padding bits are zero.

Refusals by name (`RasterError`): `NonPositiveCellSize`, `NonFiniteCellSize`, `GridTooLarge`, `EmptyGrid`, `NonFinite`, `OutOfRange`, `EmptyRegion` (`covering`), `RegionExceedsGrid` (`rasterize_over` refuses a part that does not fit, because a clipped part raster is not an over-approximation). `rasterize_free` clips freely, because a cell outside the region is never free.

No raster value reaches posted output or a verdict. The raster only filters candidates. The exact `geo2d` check decides (#2525).

## Type

`feat(geometry)`: the module is a new public API of `camcraft-geometry` for the later nest slices. No user sees it yet, and there is no caller.

## Readings (debug build, one thread)

- Part: annulus r = 50 mm, hole r = 20 mm (256 + 64 vertices), cell 0.1 mm: 1000 x 1000 cells, 662620 set, 2.3 ms.
- Sheet: 3000 x 1500 mm, cell 1 mm (the default): 3000 x 1500 cells, 4491004 free (= 2998 x 1498), 3.9 ms.

## Pinning tests (`crates/geometry/tests/nesting_raster.rs`, all pass)

- `raster_over_square_golden_and_cover`: golden counts (144 over, 64 free) and the dense-sample cover check.
- `raster_over_part_with_hole_covers_and_keeps_hole_open`
- `raster_over_thin_sliver_covers`: a 0.05 mm sliver and a 0.03 mm rotated sliver.
- `raster_over_rotated_part_covers`: a rotated rectangle and a 17-gon, at 1 mm and at 0.333333 mm.
- `raster_free_sheet_cells_inside_and_holes_not_free`: each free cell has its four corners and its centre inside, and no edge touches it (exact integer test).
- `raster_same_input_same_bits`
- `raster_packing_rows_and_padding`
- `raster_refusals_name_their_reason`
- `raster_degenerate_input_is_clean`: empty region, zero-area sliver, region outside the grid, huge coordinates, NaN.
- `raster_reading_typical_sizes`

Quick gate `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` on head `3c3b559bb`: a change to `crates/geometry/src/lib.rs` makes the quick tier fall back to batch. Result: 897 steps, 0 failed, clippy `-D warnings` clean.

## Not exercised

- The cover check uses a dense point sample, not a proof over all points. Points within 0.5 um of a cell line can round to the next cell. The sample offsets keep away from that case.
- No GPU path, no placer, no Minkowski inflation of a part (later slices of #2525).
- No release-build timing.

## MCP

No user-facing command is added, so no MCP tool is owed.

title: fix(2d): fence the whole-contour lead room at a level another band shares
body:
## What changed

- The whole-model 2D Contour now plans all its bands first and emits them at the end (new module `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_whole_fence.rs`).
- Before a band is emitted, its lead room (`PreparedBand::room`) is its center region plus a fence around each ring of another band. The fence is 0.05 mm on each side. The fence goes only around a ring that is cut on a level that this band also cuts.
- The lead fitter then shortens, reseats or refuses a lead that would cross that ring. A refusal gives a named note.
- The levels do not change. The grown ring still steps down from the stock top. At stock top 18.5 its first pass is Top Z 15, which is one stepdown under the stock top.
- An error that carries the partial path (ghost) emits the planned bands first. Thus the ghost does not change.
- `emit_band` reads `band.room` when it is set (`contour.rs`).
- The decision entry is `docs/decisions/2677-shared-level-lead-fence.md`.

## Cause

A grown outline takes the levels above its first level (`reach_up`). These levels can share a plane with a ring of an earlier band. title: feat(2d): Slot Undercut for T-slot, keyseat, dovetail and lollipop cutters
body:
## What changed

This PR adds the Slot Undercut operation and the cutters for it.

- **Four cutter kinds** in `camcraft-tools`: `t_slot`, `keyseat`, `dovetail`, `lollipop`. They use the existing tool fields. `diameter` is the head. `flute_len` is the head height. `shank_d` and `shank_len` are the neck. `tip_angle` is the dovetail flank angle. The kind words are additive, so `PROJECT_VERSION` does not change. The starter catalog has one cutter of each kind.
- **One generator** in `camcraft-motion` (`machining2d::undercut`). It cuts a straight slot or a circular slot (DXF-style bulge). It changes Z at one XY station only, outside the wall. It feeds in sideways, cuts the centre pass and the radial stepover passes at one depth, feeds out the same way, then lifts. The pass offset comes from the widest point of the cutter profile, not from the tip.
- **One verify law** in `camcraft-sim` (`Mode::Undercut`, `verify/undercut.rs`). A move that changes Z while material is in or over the head is `Warning::UndercutLift`. It blocks the post. A neck or holder band with material above its bottom is a `ShankHit`. The operation layer reads the two again against the stock that the earlier operations left (`acquit_undercut_by_prior`). A neck slot that an earlier Slot operation cut is then air.
- **The true profile in the solid law.** The solid law judges a dovetail as a frustum and a lollipop as a full ball (`Prof::Dove`, `Prof::Ball`). The head top gets the same allowance as the tip, so a head that stands under its roof is contact and not a gouge.
- **The true profile in the field stock simulation** (`Stock::simulate_undercut`). The head and the neck are two convex solids. The field keeps their union. A new exact frustum solid is `SdfTool::Dovetail`. The stock view uses this.
- **The column engines cut nothing for an undercut.** A column has one top for each (x, y). It cannot hold air below material.
- **App**: `OpParams::SlotUndercut` (kind tag 44, appended), the project file mirror, the stamp digest, heights, the part solid law for a part source, the kept-parts law for a stock source.
- **MCP**: `add_operation` with kind `Slot Undercut` (key `slot_undercut`) and `add_tool` with the new kind words. `verify` reports the new finding kind `undercut_lift`. No new MCP tool is necessary: the generic tools call the same undoable commands.
- **UI**: the tool kinds in the tool page, the operation page (`undercut_page.rs`), five original icons (SVG masters, rendered with `cargo xtask icons`).
- **Docs**: a Slot Undercut section in the 2D operations guide, and `docs/decisions/1444-slot-undercut.md`.

## Cause

There was no cutter kind with a head wider than its neck, and no operation for one. The laws for a plain contour are wrong below a roof. The column model reads a pass as a cleared kerf, so a lift through the roof passes as a retract in its own kerf.

## Tests

New pins. Each one did not exist before this PR (the code under test is new), so "red before the fix" is shown by the mutation results below.

- `camcraft-tools` `undercut::tests` (7 tests): sane cutters, refusals by name, the profile contact point, the drawn outline.
- `camcraft-motion` `machining2d::undercut::tests` (8 tests): `every_z_move_stands_at_the_entry_station`, `an_entry_slot_too_narrow_for_the_neck_is_refused_by_name`, `a_curved_slot_rides_concentric_arcs`, `the_passes_widen_to_the_wall_by_the_profile_contact_radius`, `bad_input_is_refused_by_name`, and three more.
- `camcraft-sim` `tests/undercut_laws.rs` (14 tests): `a_retract_inside_the_undercut_is_refused`, `a_dive_into_uncut_stock_is_refused`, `the_neck_through_uncut_stock_is_a_collision`, `a_slot_mouth_narrower_than_the_neck_is_a_collision`, `the_solid_law_reads_a_dovetail_as_a_frustum`, `the_solid_law_reads_a_lollipop_as_a_whole_ball`, `a_head_standing_under_its_roof_is_contact_and_one_lifted_into_it_is_a_gouge`, `the_field_removes_the_undercut_and_keeps_the_roof`, `the_field_cuts_a_dovetail_wall_on_its_slope`, `the_field_cuts_a_lollipop_groove_round`, and three more.
- `camcraft-app` `tests/mcp_slot_undercut.rs` (5 tests): a T-slot block is cut, verified and posted through the MCP tools; an end mill and a narrow entry slot are refused by name; a missing neck slot holds the post; a Z move with the head below the stock holds the post; a cut below the part floor is a gouge that holds the post.
- `camcraft-app` `tests/golden_undercut.rs` (4 tests) with four new golden CL files.
- `camcraft-app` `tests/tool_law.rs`: `undercut_cutters_mount_only_the_slot_undercut`.

Tests changed because the change extends a pinned list:

- `tool_sanity_tests.rs` and `tests/tool_law.rs`: the tool kind lists (18 to 22).
- `catalog_asset_tests.rs`: the catalog order (33 to 37 entries).
- `operation/tests.rs` (kind count 44 to 45), `lathe_voice_tests.rs` (refused count 31 to 32), `tests/ribbon.rs` (the last kind), `tests/coarse_laws.rs` (the kind is refused on a reduced model), `tests/tool_gate.rs` (the catalog hint for the new kind).
- Seven test files got the new `undercut: None` field in a full `Cutter` literal.

Mutation results (each guard removed, the pin run, the guard put back):

- M1 undercut lift law off: RED (`a_retract_inside_the_undercut_is_refused`, `a_dive_into_uncut_stock_is_refused`). Restored: GREEN.
- M2 neck and holder band law off: RED (`the_neck_through_uncut_stock_is_a_collision`, `a_slot_mouth_narrower_than_the_neck_is_a_collision`, `an_unknown_prior_height_keeps_the_conviction`). Restored: GREEN.

- M5 field neck cut with the head radius: RED (`the_field_removes_the_undercut_and_keeps_the_roof`, `the_field_cuts_a_lollipop_groove_round`). Restored: GREEN.
- M6 neck slot refusal off: RED (`an_entry_slot_too_narrow_for_the_neck_is_refused_by_name`). Restored: GREEN.
- M7 generator lifts where it stands, not at the station: RED (`every_z_move_stands_at_the_entry_station` and four more; the generator's own check refuses the path). Restored: GREEN.
- M8 part solid law off for the undercut: RED (`an_undercut_below_the_parts_floor_is_a_gouge_that_holds_the_post`). Restored: GREEN.
- M9 column engines cut the undercut as a flat mill: RED (`a_t_slot_is_cut_verified_and_posted_over_the_tools`). Restored: GREEN.
- M10 re-read against the earlier stock off: RED (`a_t_slot_is_cut_verified_and_posted_over_the_tools`). Restored: GREEN.
- Not pinned: `Rest::new` takes no cut from an undercut path. The undercut law does not read the rest model, so no test goes red without it. It keeps the rapid law from reading a pass as a cleared kerf.

Gate: the branch contains `upstream/main` 409c0b5ab (merged in, no conflict). `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on that head: 725 steps, 724 green, 1 red. The red test is `feature_edge_g1_join::no_pickable_edge_is_a_tangent_piece_of_a_longer_one_in_any_step_fixture`. It fails on `bar_cross_holes.step`, a fixture that is new on `main`. This PR does not change STEP import or feature edges. Issue #2713 reports it. Before the merge of `main`, the same gate was green on this change (716 steps, 0 failed), after one run with three red list pins that this change extends (kind count, refused count, catalog hint). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean on the final head.

## Goldens moved

No existing golden changed. Four golden CL files are new:

- `slot_undercut_tslot_straight.cl`
- `slot_undercut_keyseat_arc.cl`
- `slot_undercut_dovetail_straight.cl`
- `slot_undercut_lollipop_arc.cl`

No snapshot PNG changed. Five icon PNGs are new (`cargo xtask icons` wrote them from the new SVG masters and changed no other PNG).

## Not exercised

- **No literature search was run.** The issue asks for a Perplexity search first. This session had no web tool and no Perplexity tool. The code was written from published material that the decision file names (Machinery's Handbook for the cutter forms; Requicha and Voelcker 1982 and Frisken et al. 2000 for the union of convex solids on a distance field; the sources of the existing solid law). The maintainer can ask for the search against that list. camlib was not read.
- The UI page and the icons compile and the UI suites pass. No person looked at the page in the running app. No UI test opens the new page.
- Dovetail and lollipop parts are not tested through the app. Their profiles are tested in the sim crate (solid law and field stock) and the generator.

title: fix(machine): judge only the quarter points that an arc sweeps
body:
## What changed

`machine::judge::move_extremes` gives the points that the machine travel check judges for one move.
For an arc, it now gives the two endpoints and only the quarter points that the arc sweeps.
The sweep runs from `from` to `to` in the direction of `arc.ccw`, in the arc's own plane (XY, XZ or YZ).
The mill, lathe, plasma, waterjet and wire checks all read this one function.

The check keeps all four quarter points in two cases:

- The in-plane endpoints are 0.01 mm apart or less. Their NC words can be equal, and a control turns equal endpoints a full circle.
- The sweep reads zero or is not finite.

A four-decimal inch post has a 0.00254 mm step on each axis.
Endpoints less than 0.0036 mm apart can round to the same point on a diagonal.
The 0.01 mm bound includes margin and agrees with `ring_zig::MIN_ARC_CHORD`.

The radius is now the larger of the two endpoint radii. The old code used the radius at `from`.

## Cause

The old function added all four quarter points of the arc's full circle.
A 2D Contour cuts a gentle curve as an arc with a very large radius.
The issue's move 31 has a radius of 22170 mm and a sweep of 0.259 degrees.
The check judged points 22 m away from the tool and refused a legal program on each machine size.

## Tests

New suite `crates/app/tests/machine_arc_sweep.rs` (9 tests). It runs `machine::check_ops` on one cached move.

- `a_shallow_arc_of_a_large_radius_inside_the_stroke_passes`
- `the_same_endpoints_the_long_way_round_are_refused_on_their_own_side`
- `an_arc_is_judged_on_the_side_that_it_sweeps`
- `a_vertical_plane_arc_is_judged_on_the_side_that_it_sweeps`
- `a_quarter_point_on_an_endpoint_counts`
- `a_full_circle_keeps_all_four_quarter_points`
- `endpoints_that_post_as_one_point_keep_all_four_quarter_points`
- `endpoints_that_round_to_one_inch_point_keep_all_four_quarter_points`
- `an_arc_with_no_sweep_to_read_keeps_all_four_quarter_points`

Original evidence before the review fix: 4 of the original 8 tests fail on the code of `upstream/main` (the shallow arc, the two side tests, the no-sweep arc). The failure of the shallow arc shows the issue's symptom: `move 0 reaches 22320.200 in X, the stroke is -3000.000..3000.000`.

Original mutation results (each mutation restored, then the original suite is green, 8 of 8):

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| Old `judge.rs` from `upstream/main` | red: 4 tests fail |
| Remove the 0.001 mm endpoint guard | red: `endpoints_that_post_as_one_point_keep_all_four_quarter_points` |
| Remove the zero-sweep guard | red: `an_arc_with_no_sweep_to_read_keeps_all_four_quarter_points` |
| Ignore `arc.ccw` | red: the three side tests |

Review fix evidence: `endpoints_that_round_to_one_inch_point_keep_all_four_quarter_points` passes with `SAME_WORD = 0.01`.
Reverting only `SAME_WORD` to 0.001 makes this test fail with `MachineCheck { problems: [] }`.
Restoring 0.01 makes the test pass again.

Review fix gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green.
All four steps pass: app build, app lib, `fourth_axis_pose`, and `machine_arc_sweep`.
Review fix clippy: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

Original gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green (app lib, `fourth_axis_pose`, `machine_arc_sweep`).
These suites are green too: `vmc_stroke`, `machine`, `lathe_stroke`, `lathe_thread_travel`, `plasma_machine`, `waterjet_machine`, `edm_machine`.
`cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

title: fix(post): LinuxCNC and Tormach probe programs stop before G10 L20 when a work offset is rotated
body:
## What changed

- `assets/posts/tormach.cps` and `assets/posts/linuxcnc.cps` write a run-time guard before each `G10 L20` that writes X or Y.
- The guard tests the XY rotation register of the section's work offset and of the target work offset.
- If a rotation is not zero, the program shows a message that names the work offsets and ends with `M2`. The offset is not written.
- A result that sets only Z has no guard. A measure-only result has no guard.
- `linuxcnc.cps` now keeps the number of the section's work offset (`wcsIndex`), as `tormach.cps` already does.

```
o903 if [[#5230 NE 0] OR [#5250 NE 0]]
(MSG, PROBE: G54 OR G55 XY ROTATION NOT ZERO - NO OFFSET WRITTEN)
M2
o903 endif
G10 L20 P2 X[#5420-#190] Y[#5421-#191]
```

## Cause

- The write `G10 L20 P<n> X[#5420-#190]` gives "target = active offset + deviation" (#2610). That proof holds for work offsets without rotation.
- LinuxCNC keeps an XY rotation for each work offset (`R` of `G10 L2`, parameter 5210 + 20 x the system number).
- If the target has a rotation that differs from the active system's, the written origin depends on the machine position. The target is correct at the probe position only. This is wrong by algebra (see `docs/decisions/2683-probe-rotated-wcs.md`).
- If the two rotations are equal, the result depends on a control rule that the public LinuxCNC reference does not state: what `G10 L20` keeps for an axis that has no word. I did not confirm this rule on a control.
- The post cannot read the rotation at post time. Only the program can test it.

The issue said that the defect also applies when the target is the active work offset. I did not confirm that part. The guard also covers it, because the rule is not stated. The decision file says how to relax the guard after a run on a control.

## Tests

New file `crates/post/tests/probe_rotated_wcs.rs`. Each test runs the two posts.

- `setting_the_active_offset_stops_when_it_is_rotated`
- `setting_another_offset_stops_when_either_is_rotated`
- `the_guard_follows_the_sections_work_offset`
- `the_guard_is_written_once_under_its_own_o_number`
- `a_z_only_result_and_a_measure_only_result_have_no_guard`

Red before the fix: yes. On unchanged code the three guard tests failed, because no guard line was before `G10 L20`.

Mutation results:

- Old `tormach.cps` from `upstream/main`: 3 tests red. Restored: green.
- Old `linuxcnc.cps` from `upstream/main`: 3 tests red. Restored: green.
- `wcsIndex = n;` removed from `linuxcnc.cps`: `the_guard_follows_the_sections_work_offset` red. Restored: green.
- `if (xy)` changed to `if (true)` in `tormach.cps`: `a_z_only_result_and_a_measure_only_result_have_no_guard` red. Restored: green.

Gate, on base `3a240b7fb` (the `upstream/main` of the start of the work):

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 653 steps, 0 failed, 36.9 min. The changed shared golden made the plan run each app suite.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. No Rust file of another crate changed.
- `upstream/main` moved to `75e74a9cb` during the gate. `git merge-tree` shows a clean merge, and no commit in that range changes a file of this PR. I did not run the gate again on the new base.

## Goldens moved

Six goldens changed. Each one got the same four guard lines directly before its `G10 L20` line, and no other line changed (`git diff upstream/main -- "*.nc"`: 24 insertions, 0 deletions).

- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach/probe_edge.nc` (`o902`)
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach/probe_corner.nc` (`o903`)
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach/probe_bore_centre.nc` (`o903`)
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach/probe_boss_centre.nc` (`o903`)
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach/probe_bore_centre_mm.nc` (`o903`)
- `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/tormach/probe.nc` (`o903`)

`probe_face.nc` did not change, because a face result sets only Z.

## Not exercised

- No program ran on LinuxCNC, PathPilot or PathPilot Hub. The words `NE` and `OR`, and the parameters `#5230`.., are from the LinuxCNC G-code reference as I know it. I could not open the reference from this machine (the network call was not permitted).
- No test runs the program in a controller model. #2682 owns that model.
- The guard message was first `... OFFSET NOT SET`. `probe_tormach.rs` reads each word that starts with `S` as a spindle word, so I changed the text and did not change that test.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes `tormach.cps`, `linuxcnc.cps` or the probe tests.

Changelog: The Tormach and LinuxCNC probe programs stop with a message, and write no work offset, when a work offset that they use has an XY rotation.

title: feat(import): cadmpeg runner with version check and temp-dir sandbox
body:
## What changed

- `crates/app/src/geometry/import/native.rs` is new. It holds the shared qualified-extension table. The table is empty. Each native CAD extension that is not in the table is refused by name. This includes IGES and `.prt`.
- `crates/app/src/geometry/import/cadmpeg/` is new. It runs the external `cadmpeg` program and gives the STEP text to the STEP importer.
  - It uses the stated path first. If no path is stated, it searches `PATH`.
  - It requires version `0.6.12` or newer.
  - It runs `cadmpeg check --json <input>`.
  - It runs `cadmpeg convert <input> -o <out> --to step --reject-lossy=export`. It never gives `--allow-errors`.
  - The file path is one argument of the child process. No shell runs.
  - Each run uses a private folder below the temp folder. A `Drop` guard removes the folder.
  - A time limit stops the child. A 16 MiB limit applies to the output that the child prints. `MAX_FILE_BYTES` applies to the STEP file.
- `ImportModel::checked_budget` uses the table. The hardcoded `"iges" | "igs"` arm is removed.
- `ViewPrefs` has the new optional field `cadmpeg_path` (`cadmpegPath` in `camcraft-prefs/1`). The key is written only when it is set. Older files load unchanged.
- The UI keeps a stated `cadmpegPath` when it saves the preferences. No UI control sets the path. That is the work of #1876.
- The module `cadmpeg` is compiled only when the target is not `wasm32`.

No shipped import reaches the runner now, because the table is empty. #1875 adds the formats.

## Cause

This is new work for #1572. It is not a defect fix.

## Deviation from the issue

The issue asks for a `cadmpeg formats --json` probe. cadmpeg 0.6.12 does not have this option. `formats` prints a text table only. The first worker on this issue reported this.

This PR does not parse that table. The exit status of `check` and of `convert` is the capability test. A build that cannot read the format or cannot write STEP fails one of the two commands, and the import is refused with the last error line of cadmpeg. `docs/decisions/1873-cadmpeg-runner.md` records this decision and four others. The maintainer can reject it.

## Tests

New suite `crates/app/tests/cadmpeg_import.rs` (13 tests). It uses the stand-in program `testdata/stubs/cadmpeg_stub.sh`. The stub tests are `#[cfg(unix)]`.

- `unqualified_native_extensions_are_refused_by_name`
- `a_qualified_extension_routes_to_the_converter`
- `stub::a_converted_part_imports_through_the_step_importer`
- `stub::the_program_is_found_on_the_search_path_when_no_path_is_set`
- `stub::a_missing_program_is_refused_naming_cadmpeg_and_the_extension`
- `stub::an_old_version_is_refused_by_number`
- `stub::a_failed_check_is_refused_and_nothing_is_converted`
- `stub::a_blocking_finding_is_refused_even_with_exit_status_zero`
- `stub::a_hung_program_is_stopped_at_the_time_limit_and_its_folder_removed`
- `stub::a_failed_or_empty_conversion_is_refused`
- `stub::an_oversized_step_is_refused`
- `stub::output_past_the_capture_limit_stops_the_program`
- `stub::garbage_output_is_refused_by_the_step_importer`

Other pins:

- `view_prefs`: `cadmpeg_path_survives_a_restart_and_old_preferences_still_load`. The test `offline_only_survives_and_the_file_stores_zero_keys` has the new key in its key list.
- `camcraft-ui` lib: `prefs_door::a_pick_keeps_the_stated_cadmpeg_path`.

Red before the change: the pins did not compile on `upstream/main` (`import::native`, `import::cadmpeg` and `ViewPrefs::cadmpeg_path` did not exist).

Mutation results. Each guard was removed, the pin was red, the guard was restored, the pin was green.

| Guard removed | Red test |
|---|---|
| `from_json` reads `cadmpegPath` | `cadmpeg_path_survives_...`, `offline_only_survives_...` |
| blank path filter in `from_json` | `cadmpeg_path_survives_...` |
| unqualified refusal in `checked_budget` | `unqualified_native_extensions_are_refused_by_name` |
| stated path must be a program file | `a_missing_program_is_refused_...` |
| minimum version | `an_old_version_is_refused_by_number` |
| `check` exit status | `a_failed_check_is_refused_...` |
| blocking findings count | `a_blocking_finding_is_refused_...` |
| report that is not JSON | `a_blocking_finding_is_refused_...` |
| time limit | `a_hung_program_is_stopped_...` |
| stop of the child at a limit | `a_hung_program_is_stopped_...` (process id check) |
| capture limit | the capture-limit test |
| STEP size limit (loop and final check) | `an_oversized_step_is_refused` |
| `convert` exit status | `a_failed_or_empty_conversion_is_refused` |
| empty output | `a_failed_or_empty_conversion_is_refused` |
| folder removal in `Drop` | 9 stub tests (folder count) |
| UI save keeps the path | `a_pick_keeps_the_stated_cadmpeg_path` |

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green: 44 steps, 0 failed. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Goldens moved

None. `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty.

## Not exercised

- No real cadmpeg ran. It is not installed here. The command line comes from the public help text and README of cadmpeg 0.6.12.
- No real `check --json` report was read. The runner trusts the exit status and also scans each `findings` list for severity `error` or `blocking`.
- Windows and macOS did not run. The stub tests are Unix only.
- The `wasm32` build did not run. The target is not installed here.
- The path from `ImportModel::within` to the runner is not reached while the table is empty. The tests call `cadmpeg::load_open_within` and `native::route_in` directly.
- Only the direct child is stopped at a limit. A grandchild process is not stopped (decision 3).

## Overlaps

No open PR changes the same function.

- #2664 adds one line to the module list of `crates/app/src/geometry/import/mod.rs`. It touches the same file, different lines; whichever merges second refreshes.
- #2665 appends code to the end of `crates/app/src/prefs.rs`. It touches the same file, different function; whichever merges second refreshes.

## Notes

- The MCP tool and the script verb do not change. #1877 owns them. This PR adds no command.
- The stub is committed with mode `100755`. The tests link to it, so no test writes a program file.

Changelog: An import can convert a native CAD file to STEP through the optional `cadmpeg` program (version check, private temp folder, time and size limits); no format is enabled yet, and each native extension is refused by name.

Effort: max

Fixes #1873

title: fix(model): a linked model's digest is of the bytes the import parsed
body:
A linked model's SHA-256 now comes from the same read of the file that the import parsed. Before, the import read the file, parsed it, then read it again for the digest: a file that changed between the two reads recorded the newer digest over the older mesh, and the change was never imported (#2689, found in the review of #2563).

## What changed

- **One read** (`crates/app/src/geometry/import/sourced.rs`, new, native only): `load_model_open_sourced` returns the graded mesh and the digest of the bytes it parsed.
  - OBJ, STEP and `.sc`: the buffer that is parsed is hashed.
  - STL keeps its streaming parse (M5.3 E: the file never coexists with its triangles). A reader hashes every byte it hands to the parser. The ASCII path rewinds to byte 0 once after the sniff; the rewind starts the hash again. Any other seek is refused, so the digest is always of one pass. Bytes after the last binary facet, if the file grew, go into the same pass.
  - Same size cap and the same verdicts as `load_model_open_within`, which stays for the browser build.
- **`ImportModel::within`** uses it on native builds; the browser build records no link, as before.
- **Kernel SHA-256 in pieces** (`crates/kernel/src/solidcraft/sha256.rs`): `Sha256::new / update / finish_hex`; `hex_digest` is that over one piece. Re-exported as `camcraft_geometry::solidcraft::Sha256`.
- **The link check** (`model_source::read`) hashes the file in 1 MiB pieces. Before, it read the whole file into memory each time a linked file changed, which for a large STL broke the same memory law.
- `stl.rs`: `parse_stream` and `READ_BUF_BYTES` become `pub(super)` for the new module; no other change (the file is over the line limit, so the new code is in its own file).

Decisions: `docs/decisions/2689-one-read-digest.md`.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/kernel/src/solidcraft/sha256.rs` `pieces_hash_as_the_whole`: every split (1, 3, 55, 64, 65, 200 bytes) of lengths around the 55/56/64-byte padding edges gives the one-shot digest. The FIPS 180-4 vectors still pass.
- `crates/app/tests/model_link.rs`:
  - `the_link_digest_is_of_the_one_read_the_import_parsed`: for an ASCII STL (the rewind path), a binary STL, OBJ and STEP, the import's digest and the check's streamed digest are the SHA-256 of the file.
  - `the_link_check_hashes_a_file_larger_than_one_piece_as_a_whole`: a 3 MiB file, read in 1 MiB pieces.
  - The 7 tests of #2463 still pass.

`cargo xtask gate quick` (as a separate user with no credentials): 898 steps, 0 failed. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-kernel -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- The race itself is not reproduced by a test: it needs a write landing during a parse. The fix removes the second read by construction; the tests pin that the digest is of the parsed read.
- Windows and Linux: not run. No platform branches.
- The browser build (`wasm32`): `web/build-app-wasm.sh` fails on `main` today, before this PR, in the link check from #2463 (`model_link_watch.rs` takes `std::time::Instant`; E0308 at `state.rs:3130`). With that one-line fix on top (a separate PR), this branch builds for the browser: `web/build-app-wasm.sh` exit 0 (Homebrew clang 23 for wasm32).

Changelog: A file that changes while CamCraft imports it is no longer missed: the linked model's digest is now of the bytes the import read (#2689).
Effort: medium
Fork synced at v0.24.0 (branch from upstream main 3a240b7fb).

Fixes #2689

title: fix(2d): check each contour tab against every cut of its level
body:
## What changed

- New module `crates/motion/src/machining2d/tab_clear.rs`. After each ring's tabs are fitted, it reads each tab's line on the ring against every other cut of the tabbed levels. The other cuts are: the other keeps of the same ring, the far part of the two keeps beside the tab, and every other ring.
- A cut nearer than the tool diameter `D` cuts into the tab. The loop is held: its tabbed levels cut nothing. A `tabs:` note names the tab and the distance.
- A cut between `D` and `W + D` away leaves the tab at its width. A `tabs:` note names the tab and the width of the strip beside it. The moves do not change.
- `tab_bridge.rs`: a `tabs:` note when the first tab grows back over a picked start. The note names the pick and the point where the tabbed levels start.
- `contour.rs`: one line. The fits of all rings are made before the level loop.
- No posted move changes for a program that gets no new note.

## Cause

The bridge check compared only the two cuts beside a tab. It read the last `W + D` of one walk and the first `W + D` of the next walk. A later run of the same ring, or a different ring, was not read.

## Shape-mask result (on upstream/main `1ae4d061f`)

Tool 6 mm, tab width 4 mm, outside contour, no leads, 0.1 mm grid.

| Case | Distance between the two cuts | Neck of the tab | Note before |
|---|---|---|---|
| U-turn, 10 mm notch | 4 mm | 0.00 mm | none |
| U-turn, 14 mm notch | 8 mm | 1.89 mm | none |
| Second ring, parts 10 mm apart | 4 mm | 0.00 mm and 0.74 mm | none |
| Second ring, parts 14 mm apart | 8 mm | 1.89 mm | none |

A bridge is narrower than the tab width, so the issue is now `P1`.

## Tests

Pins in `crates/motion/tests/contour_tab_necks.rs` (new) and `crates/motion/tests/contour_tab_bridge.rs`:

- `a_tab_that_a_u_turn_of_its_ring_cuts_into_holds_the_loop`
- `a_tab_that_a_second_ring_cuts_into_holds_the_loop`
- `a_tab_beside_a_narrow_strip_is_named`
- `a_tab_with_room_beside_it_has_no_note`
- `the_meter_reads_the_tab_width_on_a_plain_part`
- `a_tab_that_grows_over_a_picked_start_says_so`
- `every_tabbed_level_keeps_the_tab_width` (three tabbed levels)
- `the_bridge_holds_on_the_true_arcs_to_a_tenth_of_a_micron`

Mutation results:

- Old `contour.rs` (from `upstream/main`): the U-turn pin, the second-ring pin and the strip pin are red. The meter reads necks of 0.0 mm. With the fix they are green.
- `moved_start` returns no note: `a_tab_that_grows_over_a_picked_start_says_so` is red. With the fix it is green.
- `every_tabbed_level_keeps_the_tab_width` and `the_bridge_holds_on_the_true_arcs_to_a_tenth_of_a_micron` add coverage. They are green on unchanged code too.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green, 160 steps, 0 failed, 41 min. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

The tab neck meter is `crates/motion/tests/common/tab_neck.rs`. `shape_mask.rs` has 409 lines, so the meter has its own file.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- `SLACK = 1e-6` did not change. A margin grows each tab window on a straight wall and moves the recorded router example program. The test reads the bridge on the posted arcs in chords of `1e-5` mm, and no bridge is under the tab width by more than `1e-4` mm. The decision file gives the bound. The reviewer can ask for the margin.
- `contour.rs` still calls `lead_held` on the first keep when that keep is not at the pick. The new note says that the start moved. A picked start with tabs permits only no lead or a perpendicular lead.
- Inside contours and leads are not in the new neck tests. The reviewer's 60 x 7 mm inside slot was not run. By the rule, its two runs are 2.06 mm apart, which is less than `D`, so the loop is held with the note.
- The check is local to the tab. It does not follow a stock strip that becomes narrow away from the tab.
- The build used no compile cache: `sccache rustc -vV` did not return on this machine. The gate ran with `CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1`.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes these files.

## Review fixes

Commit `57756c69a` (owner-account takeover, ordered by the maintainer) fixes the two findings of the review of head `edb566d33`:

- `tab_clear::departed` reads a keep that turns back toward its tab before it is `W + D` away (a shallow notch). With one keep, its leads are read the same way. Pin: `a_tab_that_a_u_turn_in_a_shallow_notch_cuts_into_holds_the_loop`.
- `tab_clear::fit_loops` takes the tabbed levels of each loop from the depth ladder. A ring is read against a tab only when the two rings share a tabbed level. Pin: `a_ring_that_stops_above_the_tabs_does_not_hold_another_loop`.
- Quick gate on the new head: 160 steps, 0 failed. Follow-up: #2734.

Effort: high

Changelog: Contour tabs: a tab that another cut of the same level cuts into now holds its loop with a `tabs:` note; a narrow strip beside a tab and a start point that a tab covers get a note.

Fixes #2561

title: feat(3d): 3D Adaptive gets a Method choice with a Trochoidal method per level
body:
Stacked on #2149 (merge #2149 first)

## What changed

3D Pocket has a new parameter, **Method**, with the values Spiral and Trochoidal.
The Adaptive strategy reads it. The other strategies do not read it.
The default is Spiral. A Spiral operation cuts the same path and has the same stamp as before.

With Method = Trochoidal, each level of the plain ladder is cleared by trochoidal loops.
The loops are planned by the 2D Adaptive lane planner on the cutter-centre area of that level.
The ladder already makes this area: the footprint less the part above the plane, less the tool radius and the stock to leave.

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive_troch_level.rs` (new) plans, posts and checks one level.
- `crates/motion/src/machining3d/troch.rs` (new) holds the state of one run and the entry point `pocket3d_trochoidal`.
- `ladder` gets a `method` argument and four short hooks.
- `OpParams::Pocket3D` gets the field `method`. The project file writes it as the word `method` (`spiral` or `trochoidal`). A file without the word reads as Spiral.
- The stamp gets one byte only for Adaptive with Trochoidal.
- The Passes tab of 3D Pocket shows a Method row when Strategy is Adaptive.
- MCP: `edit_operation` and `add_operation` accept `"method"` in `params`. No new tool is necessary, because the method is a field of the existing parameters.
- The guide page `operations-3d.md` has one new table row and one new paragraph.

Rules of a trochoidal level:

- Each cutting move stays in the level area. The posted level is checked move by move.
- The posted level is checked against the crossing law: its own moves and all moves before it.
- A bore starts on a plane only if the run proved that plane cleared below the disc of the bore helix. If not, the bore starts one plunge height above the stock top.
- A level that the method cannot cut is cut by the Spiral plan. A note gives the reason and the Z of the level. The refused attempt posts nothing.
- In a trochoidal run, each level enters as a first level does. No level reads the plane above as cleared.
- The rest pass, the offset shells and the rotary wrap keep the plan that they had. Their existing notes say so.

## UI screenshots

These images show the real 3D Pocket Passes tab under `Strategy = Adaptive` on a 60 x 40 x 20 mm pocket block (`1440 x 960`, software/headless WGPU render).
The before capture removes only the new `Method` row and its `Trochoidal` hint arm in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/mill3d_page.rs`.
The after captures show the `Method` combo (`Spiral` default and `Trochoidal`) and the `Trochoidal` hover hint on the `Method` label.
The screenshots live only on the fork's `pr-screenshots` branch at `871b8c1fec9376b3eb26d8af94a86fc4f325e7ee`.

| Before | After (`Method = Spiral`, default) | After (`Method = Trochoidal`, hint shown) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![Before: 3D Pocket Passes tab under Adaptive without Method row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/871b8c1fec9376b3eb26d8af94a86fc4f325e7ee/2704/before.png) | ![After: 3D Pocket Passes tab under Adaptive with Method set to Spiral](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/871b8c1fec9376b3eb26d8af94a86fc4f325e7ee/2704/after-spiral.png) | ![After: 3D Pocket Passes tab under Adaptive with Method set to Trochoidal and hint tooltip](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/871b8c1fec9376b3eb26d8af94a86fc4f325e7ee/2704/after-trochoidal.png) |

## Cause

This is new work, not a defect. #1509 gave the Method choice to 2D Adaptive only. #1587 added the multi-lane planner that a 3D level area needs.

## Tests (pins, mutation results)

New pins:

- `crates/motion/tests/pocket3d_troch.rs`
  - `each_level_is_cleared_by_loops_inside_its_own_level_area`
  - `no_rapid_ends_under_the_top_the_run_proved_cleared`
  - `a_level_the_method_cannot_cut_is_cut_by_the_spiral_plan_and_said`
  - `a_fallback_level_under_a_fallback_level_still_enters_from_the_stock_top`
  - `a_strategy_that_is_not_adaptive_reads_no_method`
- `crates/motion/src/machining3d/troch_tests.rs`
  - `a_bore_starts_on_a_plane_only_where_its_disc_is_proved_cleared`
  - `a_refused_level_posts_nothing_and_is_said_with_its_z`
  - `the_method_is_off_for_spiral_another_strategy_and_a_run_that_is_not_plain`
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive_troch_level_tests.rs`
  - `a_level_inside_its_area_that_crosses_nothing_passes`
  - `a_cut_outside_the_level_area_is_refused_by_name`
  - `a_cut_across_an_earlier_move_is_refused_by_name`
- `crates/app/tests/pocket3d_trochoid.rs`
  - `the_trochoidal_method_stays_in_the_pocket_posts_clean_and_matches_its_golden`
  - `the_spiral_default_cuts_what_it_cut_and_another_strategy_reads_no_method`
  - `the_method_is_an_undoable_parameter_edit`
  - `a_new_3d_pocket_is_spiral_and_an_older_file_reads_as_spiral`
  - `mcp_sets_the_method_generates_verifies_and_refuses_an_unknown_word`
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/adaptive3d_method.rs`
  - `the_3d_adaptive_passes_tab_offers_the_method_and_defaults_to_spiral`
  - `a_strategy_that_reads_no_method_has_no_method_row`

Red before the change: the new suites do not compile on the base, because `pocket3d_trochoidal` and the field `method` do not exist.

The first run of the motion pin found a real defect in the first draft. The verifier reported `Crossing` between the bore helix of the upper level and the bore helix of the lower level. The fix: a proved bore starts on the proved plane, and each level is checked against all moves before it.

Mutations (each guard was broken, its pin was run, then the code was restored):

| Mutation | Pin | Result |
|---|---|---|
| M1: the cleared-disc proof accepts each level | `a_bore_starts_on_a_plane_only_where_its_disc_is_proved_cleared` | red |
| M2: the ladder does not reset the plane above | `a_fallback_level_under_a_fallback_level_still_enters_from_the_stock_top` | red |
| M3: the crossing check reads only the level's own moves | `a_cut_across_an_earlier_move_is_refused_by_name` | red |
| M4: the level-area check is off | `a_cut_outside_the_level_area_is_refused_by_name` | red |
| M5: a refused level is reported as posted | `a_refused_level_posts_nothing_and_is_said_with_its_z` | red |
| M6: a proved bore starts one plunge height above the plane | `a_bore_starts_on_a_plane_only_where_its_disc_is_proved_cleared` | red |
| M7: the generator does not dispatch to the method | `the_trochoidal_method_stays_in_the_pocket_posts_clean_and_matches_its_golden`, `mcp_sets_the_method_generates_verifies_and_refuses_an_unknown_word` | red |
| M8: the stamp does not read the method | `the_trochoidal_method_stays_in_the_pocket_posts_clean_and_matches_its_golden` | red |
| M9: the page does not draw the Method row | `the_3d_adaptive_passes_tab_offers_the_method_and_defaults_to_spiral` | red |

All pins are green on the final code.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green: 684 steps, 0 failed, 66.3 min wall. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean. The compile cache was off for these runs, because the sccache server on the machine did not answer.

## Goldens moved

None moved. One golden is new: `crates/app/tests/golden/pocket3d_trochoidal_pocket.cl` (1025 lines, 1023 moves). A second run without `WRITE_GOLDEN` matched it.

`git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` lists this one new file and no changed file.

## Not exercised

- A real part with many levels. The pins use two and three levels of box models.
- Method = Trochoidal together with "Do not touch" items (#2149). The code passes the items to the same ladder, but no test has such an item.
- Method = Trochoidal with Rest roughing through the application. The motion entry point accepts it; no pin runs it.
- A re-machining mask from an earlier operation together with the method.
- Posted G-code was not compared with a golden `.nc`. The application test posts the setup and checks that the post succeeds.
- The engagement that the loops meet where an upper level left stock. A note gives the area that each level leaves.
- Platforms other than Linux x86-64.
- The four trochoidal controls of 2D Adaptive (#1588) are not on the 3D page. The 3D method uses their defaults. See `docs/decisions/1591-adaptive3d-trochoidal.md`.

`crates/motion/src/machining3d/ladder.rs` was 434 lines on #2149 and is 448 lines now. It was above the 400-line limit before this change. This change does not split it, because #2149 changes the same function.

title: fix(sim): excuse a through hole's exit face in ThreadBore
body:
## What changed

- Added `exit: Option<f64>` to `ThreadBore` in `crates/sim/src/verify/thread_bore.rs`.
- Set `exit` to `h.through.then_some(h.floor_z)` in `thread_rims::thread_bores` (`crates/app/src/operation/thread_rims.rs`).
- Added `ThreadBore::at_exit` so `wall_radius` excuses a through hole's exit face on the minor circle band when every vertex satisfies `z <= exit + WALL_BAND` and every minor-circle vertex satisfies `z >= exit - WALL_BAND`.
- Required a present `exit` in `excused` to be finite and at or below `top`.
- Added pinning tests in `crates/sim/src/verify/thread_bore.rs`, `crates/app/src/operation/thread_op.rs`, and `crates/app/tests/thread_mill_rim.rs`, and recorded the design decision in `docs/decisions/2655-thread-through-hole-gouge.md`.

## Cause

On a through hole, `machining2d::thread_mill` extends the helix one pitch below `floor_z` so the teeth finish the thread out of the bottom exit.
The cutter spans `floor_z` during the lead-in and helix moves, which meet the bottom face triangles on the hole's minor rim.
`ThreadBore` previously knew only `top` (`entry_z`) and excused horizontal mouth facets only at `z >= top - WALL_BAND`.
Every bottom exit facet therefore returned `None` from `wall_radius`, and the solid law flagged each move with `Warning::Gouge` ("move N cuts past the finish surface").

## Tests

- Pins:
  - `thread_mill_rim::a_detected_through_hole_with_tm0600_verifies_clean_and_posts`: failed before the fix with 21 `Gouge` warnings on lead-in and helix moves; passes after the fix with clean verify, empty verification gate, zero stock-sim gouge cells, and clean Fanuc post.
  - `thread_mill_rim::a_through_hole_into_a_lower_part_still_convicts`: passes after the fix (a lower plate below the exit still convicts).
  - `verify::thread_bore::tests::a_through_hole_exit_face_is_excused_while_blind_and_shelves_are_not`: passes after the fix (tests flat and sloped exits, blind holes, intermediate shelves, lower surfaces, inner steps, major radius limits, and non-finite or inverted `exit`).
  - `operation::thread_op::tests::the_thread_grant_reads_the_threads_own_pitch_and_only_over_a_round_wall`: passes after the fix (verifies `exit` is `None` for blind holes and `Some(floor_z)` for through holes).

title: fix(post): Sodick wire skims on their own LN condition words
body:
## What changed

- `assets/posts/sodick-wire.cps` now posts a Wire Contour with skim passes. Before, it refused each skimmed contour by name (#617, #538).
  - The rough pass keeps its C word after T91, before the first move.
  - Each skim's C word comes after the previous pass's return to the threading point, before the skim's first move. The wire stays threaded. The section has one T91 and one T90. The pass links stay G01.
  - A note line names each skim and its condition.
  - A skim condition id that is not `C` and three digits is refused by name. The app writes no file.
- New boolean post option `approachCondition` (default off). When it is on, the post writes `C000` before the first approach move (threading point to the contour). The operation's C word follows that move. Skims get no C000.
- With the option off, the output for a contour without skims is byte-identical. The #617 goldens do not change.
- `assets/posts/AGENTS.md`: the sodick-wire paragraph describes the skims and the option.
- Decision entry: `docs/decisions/2649-sodick-ln-pass-structure.md`.

## Reproduction

On `main` (370d38df6), a punch with the rough condition C001 and the skims C002 and C903 does not post through the Sodick post. The post refuses with "a condition change between passes (skims) is not supported by this post". So no LN1W / LN2W 2- or 3-pass job can post.

## Sources

- Sodick Inc., "Wire EDM Machine Operation Training, LN1W / LN2W Control" (AQ400L, AQ600L, AD360L; part number 6300015, January 2012), public at fab.cba.mit.edu/content/tools/sodick_edm/sodick_user_manual_small.pdf. We used behaviour only, and we copied no text and no sample program:
  - the word list: C001 for the first cut, C002 for the second cut, C903 for the third cut;
  - the NC program example: the next pass's C word after the return to the start point, with the wire left threaded;
  - the condition header rows: C000 / H000 are named "Approach".
- The existing #617 source (Sodick 1998 "Wire EDM Machine Operation", Mark 21 / EX21) for all other words.

## Inferred, not stated by the source

- The placement of C000. The manual names the row "Approach" but shows no program line with it. For this reason, the option is off by default and applies only to the first approach move.
- Flushing for skims. The manual's example changes the flushing for the finish passes. The post writes no flushing word for a skim. Follow-up: #2686.

## Readings (new golden `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/sodick-wire/wire_slug_punch_passes.nc`)

- `T91`, then `C001`, then the rough lead-in `G01 X-20.165 Y0.`.
- After the return `G01 X-30. Y0.`: `(SKIM 1 ...)`, `C002`, then the lead-in `G01 X-20.145 Y0.`.
- After the next return: `(SKIM 2 ...)`, `C903`, then the reversed pass from `G01 X-20.135 Y0.`.
- `T90`, `M02`. There is no `G00` between T91 and T90.
- The skim lead-ins match the wire-iso skims golden (`wire_contour_punch_skims.nc`).

## Pinning tests

- `sodick_wire_passes::a_rough_cut_and_two_skims_post_each_pass_on_its_own_ln_condition` - ok
- `sodick_wire_passes::the_approach_condition_option_cuts_the_first_approach_on_c000` - ok
- `sodick_wire_passes::a_skim_condition_that_is_not_a_sodick_c_word_is_refused_by_name` - ok
- `sodick_wire_post` (8 tests, the #617 golden unchanged) - ok
- Removed: `sodick_wire_post::skims_are_refused_by_name_never_cut_on_the_rough_condition`. Skims now post, and the new file pins them.

## Golden changes

- New: `wire_slug_punch_passes.nc`.
- Changed: none. `wire_slug_punch.nc` and `wire_slug_punch_flushed.nc` stay byte-identical.

## Gate

Quick gate on e7bda5b1f (334eacd3a with `git merge origin/main` at 5c39bff51, no conflict): `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`, 589 steps, 0 failed, wall 56.4 min.

## Not exercised

- The output was not run on a Sodick LN1W / LN2W control.
- The `approachCondition` option through the post dialog UI (the host renders declared options; tested through the engine only).
- Skims combined with `edm.flushing` / `edm.tank`, and skims without automatic threading (no new code path for these).
