title: feat(deburr): picked and excluded edges, minimum edge angle, hole filter
body:
## What changed

The 3D `Deburr` operation has four new controls.

- **Picked edges.** When the source is a selection with edge chains, the operation breaks only the exposed edges on those chains. A whole model, the stock, or a selection with no edge chain keeps the automatic detection.
- **Excluded edges.** `exclude_edges` is a list of edge chains. The exposed edges on these chains stay sharp.
- **Minimum edge angle.** `min_edge_angle_deg` removes each convex crease whose face normals bend less than the value. A new operation gets 40 degrees.
- **Hole filter.** `exclude_holes`, `hole_min_diameter` and `hole_max_diameter` remove the rims of recognized round holes (`drilling::recognize`, `recognize_cross`) whose diameter is in the range.

Where the code is:

- `crates/motion/src/finishing3d/deburr_filter.rs` (new): the edge filters and their notes. `finishing3d::deburr_edges` takes the picked and the excluded chains. `deburr` calls it with no chains.
- `crates/app/src/operation/deburr_picks.rs` (new): resolves the picked and the excluded chains from the world.
- `OpParams::Deburr`, `sane.rs`, the seed, the stamp digest, the project DTO: the five new fields.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/deburr_page.rs` (new): the rows on the Deburr Geometry tab, and the button "Exclude the picked edges".

Each skipped group of edges gives a note on the toolpath. A picked chain that names no rim and no convex crease is refused by name: a vertical cone over a concave corner cuts the two faces. An excluded chain that is no longer in the model is refused by name.

## Cause

Before this change, the Deburr kernel rode each rim and each convex crease of the mesh. The operation ignored its picks: a Deburr with a selection source rode every edge of the picked models. There was no angle limit, so the facet seams of a smooth convex surface were ridden as edges.

## Decisions (`docs/decisions/1888-deburr-edge-filters.md`)

- The issue says to remove Deburr from the `!selection_drives_region` guard. I did not do that. That guard makes a 2D area from the picks and refuses an open chain. The picks are read as paths, the same as Multi-Axis Contour drive chains. The result is the behaviour that the issue asks for.
- A project file without `min_edge_angle_deg` reads 0 (every crease). That is the path the file stored. The seed for a new operation is 40. Each new key is absent from the file at its rest value, and the stamp digests a filter only off its rest value. An old automatic or face-only operation keeps its cached path unchanged. A chain-selected operation must regenerate once. Its stamp versions the changed selection behavior.
- The minimum angle and the hole filter apply to the automatic edge set only. A pick is an explicit instruction.
- A face, patch or vertex pick in the source keeps its old meaning: it names the model that the operation reads. `turned_selected_deburr_cuts_like_the_baked_part` (#2284) pins that reading. The first version of this branch refused a face pick, and the quick gate failed on that test. Only an edge chain narrows the ride.
- No new command: the new fields are operation parameters. `EditOperationParams` (UI Apply, MCP `edit_operation`) and `SetOperationGeometry` (MCP `set_operation_geometry`) carry them. No MCP follow-up issue is necessary.

## Tests (pins, mutation results)

Motion, `crates/motion/tests/deburr_filters.rs` (new, 7 tests):

- `a_crease_below_the_minimum_edge_angle_is_skipped_out_loud`
- `a_picked_chain_rides_alone`
- `a_pick_that_names_no_exposed_edge_refuses_by_name`
- `an_excluded_chain_is_left_out_of_the_automatic_edges`
- `a_hole_rim_inside_the_diameter_range_is_skipped`
- `a_cross_hole_rim_inside_the_diameter_range_is_skipped`
- `the_filter_doors_refuse_by_name`

App, `crates/app/tests/deburr_edge_filters.rs` (new, 8 tests):

- `a_picked_edge_is_the_only_edge_broken`
- `a_face_pick_names_the_model_and_keeps_the_automatic_ride`
- `an_excluded_pick_that_is_gone_is_refused_by_name`
- `an_excluded_edge_stays_sharp`
- `the_minimum_edge_angle_reaches_the_kernel`
- `a_hole_inside_the_diameter_range_keeps_its_rim`
- `the_command_door_refuses_a_bad_filter`
- `the_filters_round_trip_the_project_file`

App, `crates/app/tests/mcp_deburr.rs` (new): `deburr_takes_edge_chains_and_its_filters_through_mcp`.

Changed tests: `the_deburr_seed_carries_the_heights_and_a_hand_break_width` asserts the seed values. The UI tab table in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests.rs` names the new Geometry rows. Six test files that build `OpParams::Deburr` by hand got the new fields at their rest values.

Red before the fix: yes. The first pin did not compile on unchanged code, because the API did not exist (`gate test a_picked_chain_rides_alone`: `FAIL compile error`).

These captures render the actual shell UI meshes and textures on the CPU. The viewport is blank because Metal supplies no graphics adapter.

title: feat(deburr): a policy for edges out of the cone's reach (skip with note, or refuse)
body:
## What changed

- 3D Deburr has a new setting, `Unreachable edges`. Its values are `Skip with note` (the default) and `Refuse`.
- `finishing3d::UnreachableEdges` is a new field of `DeburrParams` and of `OpParams::Deburr` (`unreachable`).
- With `Skip with note`, the ride leaves each edge that is steeper than the flank of the cone. The note gives the count. This is the behaviour of each earlier Deburr.
- With `Refuse`, the generator refuses the operation when one edge in the window is out of reach. The message gives the count, names the setting, and names `Skip with note` as the solution. No path is made.
- The project file has the key `"unreachable": "skip_with_note" | "refuse"` in the `deburr` params. An earlier file without the key reads as `skip_with_note`. There is no `PROJECT_VERSION` step.
- The parameter digest writes one byte for `Refuse` only. The stamp of each earlier Deburr does not change.

- MCP needs no new tool. `add_operation` and `edit_operation` take `unreachable` in the params patch. `get_job` and `list_operation_types` show the field.

The kernel always skipped a steep edge with a note. The user had no setting to make this a refusal.

title: feat(tools): a plasma torch row carries a cut-data recipe by material and thickness
body:
This PR is slice 1 of #1521, the tool side only. It does not close the issue.

## What changed

- A plasma torch cutting row can carry a recipe: `CuttingRow::plasma`, type `tools::plasma_cut::PlasmaCutData`.
- The recipe key is the material of the row and the plate thickness of the recipe.
- The recipe states the kerf. These values are optional: cut height, pierce height, pierce delay, transfer height, puddle jump (percent and dwell), amperage, arc voltage, pierce capacity (`max_pierce_thickness`) and an edge-start mark.
- A blank value means "the controller's own table". There is no default value.
- The tool door (`refusal_for_kind`) refuses a bad recipe by name. `AddTool`, `ChangeTool`, the project file and the tool library all use that door.
- `plasma_row_for(rows, material, thickness)` picks a recipe. The thickness must be exact.
- Selection by material alone (`row_for`, `row_in_tool`, the `Unknown` row) ignores a recipe.
- The project file and the tool library write the recipe under the additive key `cutting_data[].plasma`. The MCP tools `add_tool` and `edit_tool` use the same JSON form.
- The tool editor keeps a recipe in the draft. It does not show the recipe as a material row.
- No toolpath and no posted output changes.

## Cause

The torch had a kerf width and no cut data. The three pierce values were on the operation. The values had no material key and no thickness key.

## Refusals

- A plasma recipe on a tool that is not a torch.
- A thickness or a kerf that is not above zero.
- A stated amperage, arc voltage, pierce capacity or puddle-jump percent that is not above zero.
- A stated height, pierce delay or puddle-jump dwell that is negative or not finite.
- A puddle jump without a pierce height.
- A row without a material, with an rpm that is not 0, or with a feed that is not above zero.
- The same material and thickness two times.
- A plate thicker than the pierce capacity, unless the recipe states an edge start.
- An unknown key in the `plasma` object of a file.

## Tests

Pins (13 new tests):

- `crates/tools/tests/plasma_cut.rs`: 8 tests, for example `plasma_recipe_thicker_than_the_pierce_capacity_needs_an_edge_start`, `plasma_recipe_is_picked_by_material_and_exact_thickness_only`, `plasma_recipe_refuses_bad_numbers_by_name`.
- `crates/app/tests/plasma_cut_data.rs`: `plasma_recipe_commands_refuse_bad_rows_by_tool_name_and_undo_restores`, `plasma_recipes_roundtrip_project_and_library_and_never_seed_by_material_alone`, `plasma_recipe_files_refuse_a_misspelt_key_and_an_unpierceable_plate`.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_cutting_rows.rs`: `a_torch_recipe_rides_the_draft_and_is_not_drawn_as_a_material_row`, `torch_material_row_button_counts_plain_rows_only`.

Red before the change: yes. On `upstream/main` 4d4a81fcf the tools pin does not compile. `CuttingRow` has no field `plasma` and the module `plasma_cut` does not exist.

Mutation results: 25 mutations, one for each guard. Each mutation made a pin fail. Each pin passed after the restore.

- Tools door: torch-only guard; recipes judged by the plain-row law; recipe law not called; `row_for` takes a recipe; `is_unknown` counts a recipe; nearest thickness.
- Recipe law: capacity guard (tools pin and app pin); edge start ignored; capacity exclusive; puddle jump without pierce height; duplicate key; thickness and kerf check; above-zero check; zero-or-more check; zero refused; rpm; feed; material; unknown file key.
- App: `row_in_tool` takes a recipe; the file drops the recipe on write; the file drops the recipe on read.
- UI: the table draws a recipe row; `add_row` counts a recipe.

The first run of the `is_unknown` mutation passed. I added one assertion to `plasma_recipe_never_stands_in_for_the_unknown_row`. The mutation then failed.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green, 13 steps, 0 failed. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Review fixes

- The `Add material row` button counts only plain material rows. Plasma recipes do not fill the plain-row table.
- UI pin: `torch_material_row_button_counts_plain_rows_only`. The test checks that the button is enabled when each material has a recipe and no plain row.
- Mutation check: the old recipe-inclusive count makes the UI pin fail (RED). The restored plain-row count passes (GREEN).

## Tool editor screenshots

Both images use the same torch draft. Each `WorkMaterial::ALL` entry has a plasma recipe. The draft has no plain material rows.
The recipes stay hidden in this editor. Before the fix, `Add material row` is disabled. After the fix, it is enabled.
The images show the actual egui component, captured with a CPU renderer because no GPU adapter was available. The temporary capture code was removed.
The images are stored only on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch, commit `cb43e7aa5900643f07e9c33027152aa8fd4d6acf`.

Before:

![Tool editor before the fix](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/2681/before.png)

After:

![Tool editor after the fix](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/2681/after.png)

## Not exercised

- No operation reads a recipe. The plasma operation, the Tormach post and the simulation are not changed.
- The recipes have no editor on the tool page. A recipe enters through the project file, the tool library or the MCP tool definition.
- The MCP path has no test of its own. It calls `project::tool_from_json`, which the app pin tests.
- The project file version has no step. An older build drops the `plasma` key and reads the row as a plain material row of the torch. `docs/decisions/1521-plasma-cut-data.md` gives the reason. Slice 2 must take the step.
- Nothing ran on a real machine. The test values are synthetic.

Work that stays open on #1521: the row pick and the overrides on the operation, generation and post (slice 2), gas type and pressure, the recipe editor, laser, waterjet pierce stages, docs and example rows.

- #2663 and this PR both change `cutting_rows` in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_cutting_rows.rs`. The PR that merges second takes a refresh.
- #2668 changes `crates/app/src/cutting_rows.rs`. This PR does not change that file.
- #2563 and #2641 change `crates/app/src/lib.rs` at other lines.

The decision record is `docs/decisions/1521-plasma-cut-data.md`.

Changelog: A plasma torch can store cut-data recipes for each material and plate thickness (heights, pierce delay, puddle jump, amperage, pierce capacity); a plate thicker than the pierce capacity is refused unless the recipe states an edge start.

Slice of #2007: the tool profile page only (parts C, D and E). The property grid (#2014) and the own modal (#2397) are not in this PR. FlamingFireCoding holds live claims on them.

## What changed

**C - one preview.** The Profile tab had a second side view of the tool, at a different scale. This PR removes it. The one to-scale preview beside the tool fields now draws the draft of the tab:
- Draw holder, Custom: a holder outline that validates shows as the bands that the collision check sweeps (`tool_body::stack`, #2017).
- Draw cutter: a cutter outline that validates replaces the steel outline. The holder goes on top of it as bands.
- A draft that does not validate shows the holder in use. Its refusal stays in red under the table.
- All other tabs show the holder in use, as before.

The new function `tool_profile_page::preview_inputs` is the one place that selects what the preview draws. `tool_preview::draw` takes an optional steel outline.

**D - clipped rows.** I saw the cause in the running app before the change. Two causes:
- egui gives a nested scroll area only the space that is left in the view (`egui-0.36.2/src/containers/scroll_area.rs`). When the table was low on the scrolled page, it fell to its 64 px least height and showed about two rows. The table now has a least height equal to its greatest height (150 px). A short table still shrinks to its rows.
- The egui `Grid` has a 40 px least column width by default. The six columns were about 300 px wide in a 260 px column, so in a narrow pane the "×" buttons were outside the pane. The grid now has no least column width.
- The tab row (Body, Profile, Draw holder, Draw cutter) and the three file buttons now wrap in a narrow column.

**E - plain words, on this page only.**
- "landed: ..." is now "In use: ...". Examples: "In use: the holder cylinder from the dimensions", "In use: library holder BT30 ER20", "In use: a drawn cutter outline".
- The table headers are "#", "height mm", "radius mm" and "arc". Each header has a hover text.
- The holder line reads "holder Ø 44.0 × 35.0 mm, from 55.0 to 90.0 mm above the tip".
- The note reads "The holder is a turned shape: you edit one half of its outline. Parts that are not round are covered by a larger safe shape, never cut away."
- The hover texts of Parametric, Custom and Apply profile use plain words.

`tool_settings.rs` has one edit of three lines: the preview call takes the output of `preview_inputs`. No other change goes into that file.

Each edit still goes through the undoable commands that the page used before (Apply profile, Apply cutter). This PR adds no command.

Decision: `docs/decisions/2007-tool-profile-one-preview.md`.

## Screenshots

Empty project, catalog tool EM-0600-4FL, Properties pane at 1600 x 1000.

- `page_layout::layout_page_tool_profile` (new). It is the named layout test of the page. In a narrow pane, the tab row, each "×" and the file buttons stay in the leaf. In the default window, the line under the table starts below the last row. I removed each part of the fix one at a time, and the test failed each time:

title: fix(post): drill and thread ops take the tool feed; a feed above it is refused at the post
body:
## What changed

- New module `crates/app/src/operation/feed_rating.rs`. It gives the feed that a tool states for a hole operation:
  - the cutting-data row of the tool and the stock material, if a row is in force;
  - else `tool.feed`.
- A Drill operation takes that feed for `feed` and `plunge_feed`. A Thread operation takes it for `feed` and caps `plunge_feed` at it. This occurs:
  - when the operation is created (`cutting_rows::seed_feed_for_tool`: ribbon quick-add, MCP `add_operation`, the recognizer);
  - when the tool of the operation changes (`EditOperationLinks`, through the new `cutting_rows::retargeted_params`). Undo restores the old feeds.
- `posting::verification_report` has a new blocking problem. If a Drill or Thread operation feeds above the feed of its tool, the post is refused. The message names the operation, the two feeds in document units and the tool. It tells the user what to change.
  - Drill: the highest feed of the generated path. Tap cycles are not judged here, because their feed is rpm x pitch.
  - Thread: the higher of `feed` and `plunge_feed`, stated at the cutting edge.
- A saved project keeps its feeds on load. A project with a feed above the tool opens, and the post refuses it with the message. The project file format does not change (no version step).
- Decision entry: `docs/decisions/2598-hole-op-tool-feed.md`.

## Readings

- Cause: each new operation got the default feeds 1200 / 300 mm/min. The feed seed changed only milling kinds with a named material row. Nothing compared the feed of a hole operation with its tool. A drill was posted at F300 with a tool that states 115 mm/min.
- Reproduction: `hole_feed_rating` failed on `origin/main` (drill at 1200/300, Thread at 1200, verify clean, post written).

## Pinning tests (`crates/app/tests/hole_feed_rating.rs`, MCP client)

- `drill_and_thread_mill_take_the_tool_feed_and_post_it`: the drill takes 115/115 from DR-0600 and the Thread takes 400 from TM-0600-P125. The Fanuc post has the drill cycle at F115. No F word is above 400.
- `a_feed_above_the_tool_is_refused_at_the_post_by_name_and_kept_on_load`: a user feed of 1200 is accepted as an edit and is undoable. Verify names the two operations. The post is refused and writes no file. Save and open keep the feeds, and the post is still refused. Feeds at the tool's value post again.
- `setting_a_new_tool_takes_its_feed_and_undo_restores_the_old_one`: `set_tool` to DR-0300 gives 120/120. Undo gives the old 90/80.

All 3 pass.

## Fixtures and examples (second commit)

These gave a hole operation a feed above its tool. Each now states the feed of its tool:
- tests: `lathe_workholding_kinds`, `setup_align_hole_kinds`, `stock_source_holes_support/mod.rs`, `tool_cutting_rows`, `wcs_rotation_control`, `first_router_part`.
- `tool_cutting_rows`: the drill assertion now expects the tool feed (410/410) and not the row feed.

## Golden changes

- `examples/catalog/2d/first-part/first-part.nc`: 4 lines, `G83 ... Q6. F300` -> `F115` (the four holes at X+-38 Y+-23). `build.camscript` sets the Drill1 feeds to 115. The `.camproj` is rebuilt from the script.
- `examples/first-part.nc`: 4 lines, `G73 X+-38. Y+-23. Z-1. R22. Q18. F300` -> `F115`. In `examples/first-part.camproj` only the two Drill1 feed values change.
- `examples/first-router-part.nc`: 1 line, `G73 X53 Y50 Z-14.803 R0 Q4 F150` -> `F115`. `examples/first-router-part.camproj` is saved again from its command build (`WRITE_GOLDEN=1`, decision of #1917). Against main it differs only in: the Drill1 `feed` and `plunge_feed` (150 -> 115) and the 16 cached drill moves (`"feed": 150.0` -> `115.0`); the stamps of Drill1, 2D Pocket1 and 2D Contour1 (the pocket and contour stamps read the drill, so a hand edit of only the drill makes them stale); and `"version"` 71 -> 72 (the current `PROJECT_VERSION` on main).
- `site/content/guide/getting-started/first-router-part.md`: the drill feed text is now 115 mm/min and the quoted G73 line has F115.
- No CL golden and no snapshot PNG changes.

title: fix(2d): cut a level at the tab top so a contour tab is tab_height tall
body:
Stacked on #2659 (merge #2659 first)

This branch is the head of #2659, then a merge of `main`, then one commit for #2579. The head of #2659 is 73 commits behind `main`, and the fix needs files that are only on `main`. The commit of this PR is `ff0f33d93`.

## What changed

- `ContourParams::ring_levels` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_params.rs`) gives the stepdown levels of a closed ring. When the operation has tabs, it adds a level at `bottom_z + tab_height`, if no level is there.
- A level within 1e-6 mm of the tab top becomes the tab top itself.
- The closed contour (`contour_region.rs`) and the whole-model contour (`contour_whole.rs`) read `ring_levels`.
- The open runs have no tabs. They keep `levels` and get no new pass.
- A tab top at Top Z or above it adds no level. Each level carries the tabs then.
- Decision entry: `docs/decisions/2579-tab-height-level.md`.

## Cause

A level carries the tabs when it is below `bottom_z + tab_height`. The last level above that plane cuts the whole ring. The tab stood up to that level. With a 4 mm stepdown and a 1.5 mm tab height, the tab was 4 mm tall. With a 1 mm stepdown, it was 2 mm tall.

A second cause gave the same result. Repeated subtraction gives a level such as `-3.0000000000000004`. That level is below a tab top at `-3.0`, so it carried the tabs. With a 0.2 mm stepdown and a 1 mm tab height, the tab was 1.2 mm tall.

## Tests

New pins, `crates/motion/tests/contour_tab_height.rs` (10 tests). They measure the tab height from the posted feed moves.

- `a_stepdown_larger_than_the_tab_height_keeps_the_tab_height`
- `a_single_level_cut_keeps_the_tab_height`
- `a_stepdown_smaller_than_the_tab_height_keeps_the_tab_height`
- `the_tab_top_level_is_one_more_level_in_the_ladder`
- `a_level_one_float_step_under_the_tab_top_is_the_tab_top`
- `a_whole_model_contour_keeps_the_tab_height`
- Controls: `a_level_already_at_the_tab_top_adds_no_level`, `a_tab_as_tall_as_the_cut_adds_no_level`, `no_tabs_adds_no_level`, `an_open_chain_has_no_tabs_and_gets_no_tab_level`

Red before the fix, on `upstream/main` `136f19763`:

```
tab height 4 is not 1.5 (stepdown 4, levels [-4.0, -8.0])
tab height 2 is not 1.5 (stepdown 1, levels [-1.0, -2.0, -3.0, -4.0])
tab height inf is not 1.5 (stepdown 4, levels [-4.0])
```

Mutation results. Each mutation was restored, and the 10 tests were green again.

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| `contour_region.rs` from `upstream/main` | red: 5 tests |
| `contour_whole.rs` from `upstream/main` | red: `a_whole_model_contour_keeps_the_tab_height` |
| The near level is not moved to the tab top | red: `a_level_one_float_step_under_the_tab_top_is_the_tab_top` |

Old pins that follow the added pass:

- `crates/motion/tests/machining2d.rs` `tabs_hold_the_part_until_the_floor`: 6 plunges, not 5. The tab top at -4 is a whole ring.
- `crates/motion/tests/machining2d.rs` `contour_tabs_stand_down_the_entry_arms`: a helix can end at the tab top (`>= -4.0`). It does not go below it.
- `crates/app/tests/wall_arc_entry.rs` `the_wall_arc_stands_down_by_name_on_tabbed_levels`: 3 arc entries, not 2. The tab top at 7 is a level without tabs.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` ran 122 steps. One step was red: `motion suites: machining2d`, with the two tests above. The two tests were updated. The suite is green after that (68 passed). The full gate was not run again after that update.
`cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Goldens moved

- `examples/first-router-part.nc`: 15 lines added, none removed. They are one whole pass of `2D Contour1` at Z-9 (bottom Z-12, tab height 3 mm, stepdown 4 mm), with its approach and its retract. `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` shows this file only.
- `examples/first-router-part.camproj`: saved again with `WRITE_GOLDEN`, as its test tells. The contour cache has the same pass (249 lines) and a new stamp. The save also writes what `main` changed since the last save: `version` 68 to 71, `number` on the two tools, four `drill_undersize` warnings, and the start of the first rapid of two operations. This PR does not cause these lines. A file with only the new pass does not pass the verification gate of `first_router_part_project_loads_verifies_and_posts_to_grblhal`.

## Not exercised

- The UI. No UI code changed.
- A tab level together with a band boundary inside the tab height (#2562).
- Keep-down level links together with the new level. The link rule reads the same tab test as before.
- A machine. The readings are from the posted moves.
- The batch tier and the release tier.

- #2659 changes `contour_whole_bodies_with` in `contour_whole.rs`. This PR changes one line of the same function (`p.levels()` to `p.ring_levels()`). `reach_up` of #2659 reads the same `flat` levels, so it can add the tab top level to a new outline. `contour_whole_new_outline` and `contour_whole` are green on this branch.
- #2149 touches `levels.rs`. This PR does not change that file.

Changelog: 2D Contour tabs are as tall as Tab height for any stepdown: the toolpath gets a pass at the tab top when the stepdown has no level there.

title: fix(face): do not lift over a hole that is below the cut plane
body:
## What changed

- A Face under the default `lift` law does not lift over a hole that is below the cut plane.
- `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs` (Face arm): under `FaceHoles::Lift` it passes the outline of the material at or above the cut plane to the facer.
- `crates/app/src/operation/material_source.rs`: new `standing_at`. It is `standing_above` read 1 um below the plane.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/face_holes.rs`: new `beside`. Under `Lift` with an outline, `forbidden` bridges a hole only when that material stands in the hole or within 0.05 mm of it.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/face.rs`: the doc comment of `face_over` says what `solid` means under `Lift`.
- A boss in a hole is lifted over as before. A bore whose rim the cut plane reaches is lifted over as before. `CutAir` and `Through` do not change. With no outline, each hole is lifted over as before.

## Cause

A model source gives the facer the silhouette of the whole part. A through-hole in a low flange is a hole of that silhouette. The facer lifted over it also when the cut plane was 5 mm above the rim of the hole.

The 16 findings of the issue were false. The path did not go below the cut plane. Each convicted move was a row piece beside a lift. Its end stood less than a tool radius from the open outer rim of the region, and verify law (b) reads each region loop as a wall for a law point. With no lift, no row end is near the rim, and the findings stop.

## Tests

Pins (red on unchanged upstream main 1ae4d061f, green with the fix):

- `face_holes_below_cut::holes_below_the_cut_plane_are_not_lifted_over` - red before: 8 plunges, expected 1, note `facing rows lifted over the region's holes at the clearance plane`.
- `face_holes_below_cut::a_face_above_holes_below_the_cut_plane_has_no_gouge_finding` - red before: `Gouge` at moves 2, 11, 14, 37, 40, 49, 52.
- `face_holes_below_cut::a_hole_whose_rim_the_cut_plane_reaches_is_still_lifted_over` - green before and after. It pins that the old law stays for a hole at the cut plane.
- `camcraft_motion::machining2d::face_holes::law::lift_bridges_only_the_holes_that_material_at_the_plane_touches` - new unit test.

Mutation results:

- Old `generate.rs` from upstream main: the first two app pins are red. Restored: green.
- Old `face_holes.rs` from upstream main: the first two app pins are red. Restored: green.
- The `(FaceHoles::Lift, Some(s))` arm removed from `forbidden`: the unit test is red. Restored: green.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on head 07d10274a is green. 118 steps, 0 failed. The plan had the app and motion lib tests and 116 suites, with `face_holes_below_cut`, `face_holes` and `face_concave_holes`. The run did not use sccache: the sccache server on this machine did not answer compiler calls.

Clippy: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- The MCP repro of the issue with the real p01-flange part. The pin uses our own flange fixture: a plate with two through-holes beside a boss.
- A tilted Face (`tilt`), and a Face with area controls (the turned frame). The code path is the one `CutAir` uses for its outline.
- The release tier and the pixel snapshots.
- A second defect stays: a lifted row end within a tool radius of the open outer rim is reported as a gouge when the hole is at the cut plane. Issue #2657 has the repro and the cause. This PR does not change that gouge law. The decision file has the reason.

## Overlaps

- #2149 and #1713 change `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`. They change other arms of `run_job_arms`, not the Face arm. The PR that merges second takes a refresh.

Decision: `docs/decisions/2437-face-holes-below-cut.md`.

Effort: high

Changelog: Face on a model source no longer lifts over holes that are below the cut plane, and verify no longer reports false gouge findings for them (#2437).

Fixes #2437

title: fix(import): hold a STEP face's facets to its surface
body:
## What changed

- The STEP importer measures the mesh that it keeps. New module `crates/app/src/geometry/import/step_fit.rs`.
- For each curved elementary face (cylinder, cone, sphere, torus), each facet edge inside the face is measured against the surface of the face.
- An edge that stands more than two pass tolerances off the surface is split at the surface. The loop ends when no edge is off.
- An edge on the boundary of a face is never split. The shell stays closed.
- A chord height that cannot be refined (facet budget, round cap) is reported as the chord error of the import. The model then has reduced fidelity (#864), and the gate refuses to verify against it.
- `step_facets::facets_of` takes the fit for each face. `step.rs` carries the remaining chord height into the chord that the import reports.

## Cause

The issue says that tilted operations are not judged for gouges. This is not the cause.

- A tilted operation is judged at generation by the keep law, in the frame of its plane. The test `a_tilted_slot_into_a_meshed_bar_is_refused` passes on unchanged `upstream/main`.
- The cause is the imported mesh of the reported part (a D50 bar with two cross holes, STEP).
- The kernel (truck) triangulates a trimmed face in its parameter plane. The parameter grid of a cylinder has two rows. The two rows are on the boundary, thus no grid point is inside the face.
- With a hole in the wall, the triangulation joined each rim edge to the rim of the hole, a quarter turn away. The facets ran through the solid, as much as 25 mm inside the true cylinder.
- The importer reported the tolerance that it asked for. It did not measure the mesh.
- The gouge laws then judged the tilted slots against a part that was too small. The slots cut "air" and posted. The upright slot was convicted only because the mesh is correct near the hole at the top.
- The defect is not limited to tilted operations. An upright cut on such a wall had the same wrong verdict.

## Tests

Pins, in `crates/app/tests/tilted_gouge.rs`:

- `a_tilted_slot_into_the_step_bar_is_refused`: the reported bar, the slot at A0, A90 and A-90. Each slot is a `Gouge` at generation. The post refuses with "cuts past the finish surface" and writes no file.
- `the_step_bars_wall_facets_lie_on_the_cylinder`: each wall facet edge of the imported bar is on the cylinder. The import reports full fidelity.
- `a_tilted_slot_into_a_meshed_bar_is_refused`: a guard. It passes before and after the fix.

Red before the fix (unchanged code):

- `the_step_bars_wall_facets_lie_on_the_cylinder`: `a wall facet edge runs 2.57401532315658 mm inside the cylinder`.
- `a_tilted_slot_into_the_step_bar_is_refused`: `S90 cuts 0.5 mm into the bar and must be a gouge: []`.

Mutation: with `step.rs`, `step_facets.rs` and `mod.rs` of `upstream/main` restored, the two pins fail as above. With the fix restored, the three tests pass.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green on the final head (22 steps: the app lib tests and 20 import and fidelity suites, 0 failed). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean. The gate ran without sccache, because the sccache server on the machine did not answer.

## Goldens moved

None. `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty.

## Not exercised

- B-spline, NURBS and swept faces are not measured (their grid is the work of #1602). The module header says so.
- Cone, sphere and torus faces with a hole have no fixture. They use the same code path as the cylinder.
- The fallback (facet budget reached, chord error reported) has no test.
- The batch and release tiers did not run. The heavy lanes did not run.
- Refinement makes many facets where the kernel mesh was wrong: the reported bar has 1 084 facets before and about 133 000 after. Its import takes about 5 s in a debug build. A better triangulation (interior rows, or a parameter stretch for elementary faces) is follow-up work; see `docs/decisions/2600-step-facets-on-surface.md`.
- The second finding of the same report (a tilt of A0 B180 with `basis_version` 0 posts its XY turned 90 degrees) is not part of this PR.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes `geometry/import/step.rs`, `step_facets.rs` or `mod.rs`.

New fixture: `testdata/models/bar_cross_holes.step` (56 kB, the part of the QA report, made in SolidCraft by the reporter).

Changelog: STEP import: a curved face with a hole in it (a bar or tube with a cross hole) no longer imports with facets that run through the solid; gouge checks on such a part, tilted or upright, now judge the true wall.

Effort: max

Fixes #2600

title: fix(2d): start a new, larger outline of a whole-model contour at Top Z
body:
## What changed

- A new file, `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_whole_reach.rs`, holds `reach_up`, `upper_levels` and `band_sweep`. When a ring of a deeper band has a tool sweep that reaches outside every sweep cut so far, `reach_up` adds levels above the ring's first level (`upper_levels`). Each pass is then at most one stepdown under the pass before it on that ring.
- `upper_levels` has three cases. The predicate is `stock_over`, the same predicate by which `cut_levels_under` keeps Top Z as a level.
  - No stock over Top Z: the flat levels under Top Z. A level at Top Z removes no material and is not added.
  - The stock top is less than one stepdown over Top Z: levels one stepdown at a time down from the stock top. These levels are off the flat grid on purpose. A pass at Top Z shares its plane with the band-0 ring there, and in `contour_whole_step` case 1 the lead of that ring crossed the grown ring (`Crossing`).
  - The stock top is one stepdown or more over Top Z: Top Z and the flat levels under it. Band 0 bites the same depth at Top Z.
- If the ring cannot be proven clear of the part at the added levels, the operation is refused by name. The toolpath is not made, so nothing posts.
- A ring whose sweep stays inside the cut sweeps is not changed (an outline that does not grow).
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_whole.rs` keeps the union of the band sweeps (`cover`) and calls `reach_up` after `check_unread`.
- Decision entry: `docs/decisions/2597-new-outline-from-top-z.md`. The stepdown is the axial limit of the operation. So there is no new parameter: its other value would post the buried pass again. The entry also records the B1 fix and the dropped options.

## Review fix B1 (second review)

- Before: with the stock top over Top Z, `reach_up` added only the levels under Top Z. On the #2597 part with the stock top 28 (Top Z 25, stepdown 5), the base ring was first cut at Z 20, 8.000 mm under the stock top.

title: fix(ui): hold the playhead while the stock removal is calculated
body:
## What changed

The playback worker calculates the full stock removal before it publishes a frame (#2181). During this time the viewport shows the uncut stock. The transport clock did not stop. The tool moved over stock that showed no cut. On a large block, the full program can play before the first cut shows. This is the "no visible stock removal" of #2611.

- `crates/ui/src/play_precalc.rs`: new `holds_playhead` (true while `Precalc::Running`) and `advance_playhead` (the transport clock step; it does nothing while the calculation runs).
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/shell.rs`: the transport uses `advance_playhead`. The scrub slider is disabled while the calculation runs. Play, Stop and Cancel still work. Cancel stops the calculation, and playback then cuts live as before.
- `crates/app/tests/stock_play_picture.rs` (new): plays the worker as the transport does, composes each frame as the eye does (`max(mesh, cut)`), and counts the solid texels. It proves that the frames show the removal, at the full budget and at the display budget.
- `docs/decisions/2611-playhead-waits-for-precalc.md`: the decision and the dropped options.

## Readings

- Without the fix, the pinning UI test fails: `the playhead waits while the stock removal is calculated`, `left: Some(0.1)`, `right: Some(0.0)`.
- With the fix, it passes (25 s).
- The two app tests pass on main and on this branch. Thus the data of the worker frames is correct, and the defect is the clock.

- No screenshots. The change holds the playhead in time; a still picture does not show it. I did not launch the GUI.

title: fix(ci): post-merge report job runs when the gate fails
body:
## What changed

The `report` job of `.github/workflows/post-merge.yml` has `needs: gate` and an `if` with no status check function. GitHub then adds an implicit `success()`. When the gate fails, the job is skipped before GitHub reads the expression. Thus a red `main` opened no rolling issue (run 43535610115, as #1611 says).

- `.github/workflows/post-merge.yml`: the `if` of the `report` job now starts with `always() &&`. The other terms do not change:
  - `needs.gate.result == 'success' || needs.gate.result == 'failure'`: a cancelled or a skipped gate still reports nothing.
  - `needs.gate.outputs.skipped != 'true'`: a run that yields to a cut still reports nothing.
  - The ref terms: a dispatch of a non-main ref still reports nothing.
- A comment on the job says why `always()` is necessary.
- No trigger, permission, runner label or step changes.

The red path after the gate already works: the gate job uploads `gate-output.txt` with `if: always()`, and `.github/scripts/post-merge-report.sh` reads `STATUS=failure` and the FAIL rows.

title: fix(app): probe reads its picks in the setup frame in a turned setup
body:
## What changed

The Probe op read the picked feature's placement from the model
(`model::transform_of`). Generation judges the stylus against the facets
of the setup frame. In a setup that holds the part turned, the two reads
disagreed: the posted cycle sought a surface 10 mm inside the part, with
no refusal and no diagnostic.

- `operation::probe_pick`: the pick's placement now comes from
  `setup_align::pose_in(world, entity, setup)`. `probe_seed`,
  `probe_from_picks` and `probe_account` take `setup: Option<&str>`, the
  shape #2276 gave the Slot helpers.
- The call sites pass the operation's setup name:
  `commands::operation::geometry` (`SetOperationGeometry`),
  `operation::picks` and `operation::selection_memo`. Both of the last
  two already had it.
- `setup_align`: `OpParams::Probe` joins the verified mill kinds
  (`verified_mill`), so Probe generates on `Mill` and `MillTurn` in an
  aligned setup. The refusal message now names Probe. Probe is not a
  turning kind: `verified_turn` is unchanged, and the lathe-post refusal
  in `lathe_voice` stays.
- Five sentinels pinned Probe as the refused kind. They now name kinds
  that are still unverified: a hand-carried `WireContour` params read
  through `generation_problem` (in the 2D-kinds, multi-axis and
  op-frame suites), a tilted Contour (the tilted-plane branch in
  `setup_align`), and the mill-turn loop. The mill-turn suite now
  asserts Probe is admitted there.

## Readings

- The generation arm already passed setup-frame facets to
  `probe_op::generate_probe` (the #2210 work). Only the seed read the
  model frame, so no other generation path needed a change.
- Probe's `KindInfo` is in `Section::Drilling`, so its family is Mill.
  One allowlist entry therefore covers `Mill` and `MillTurn`.
- The overtravel point is not a move: `probing::probe_cycle` records it
  in `path.probes` only. The moves stop at the tangent point, which is
  why a seeded touch stays clean while a stale target does not.
- The stylus law convicts a stale model-frame target because the feed
  from the safe plane crosses the turned part's top face on the way
  down.

## Pinning tests

- `setup_align_probe_kinds::turned_probe_reads_its_pick_in_the_setup_frame`
- `setup_align_probe_kinds::a_model_frame_target_in_a_turned_setup_is_convicted`

Negative control: with the old `model::transform_of` read, the first
test fails on the seed (`the turned seed: [20.0, 15.0, 10.0]`) and the
stylus law convicts that path (`Gouge` at moves 3 to 6). With the fix,
both tests pass.

## Not exercised

- No UI change: Probe was refused at generation only, so no ribbon or
  panel entry was blocked before, and none is blocked now.
- No MCP change: `set_operation_geometry` calls the same command, so it
  takes the setup-frame seed with this fix.
- A pick on a bore, boss, edge or vertex in a turned setup: every mode
  shares the one placement read that the face proof covers.
- The `Lathe` and `MillTurn` turning paths, and posts other than the
  built-in mill post.

## Notes

- The quick gate on this branch has five red binaries unrelated to the
  change, red at the branch point as well: `example_catalog`,
  `first_part_programs` and `wire_taper_angle` fail on CRLF checkouts of
  fixtures and goldens (#2523); `thread_boss` and `thread_mill` fail on
  stale NC goldens (tool numbers only). Checked: both stay red with the
  clean `origin/main` code in this same checkout.
- `crates/app/src/setup_align.rs` is already past the 400-line guide on
  `main` (457 lines). This change adds one line to it.
- `SetOperationGeometry::new` and the job-collect region also carry
  changes in the open PRs #2149 and #2134. A conflict at merge time is
  expected; this branch takes `origin/main` only at merge time.

title: feat(model): a linked model is imported again when its source file changes
body:
Builds on #2542 (#2462), which is now merged: the change to review is the commit `feat(model): a linked model is imported again when its source file changes`.

## What changed

- **A model records its source file.** An import from a file records the path and the file's SHA-256 (`schema::ModelSource`, `crates/app/src/model_source.rs`). The record rides `ImportModel`, `UpdateModel` (traded with the facets; undo restores it; a repair keeps it), `DeleteEntity` and `ImportFixture`. A mesh handed in, a browser pick and a generated fixture mesh record none.
- **Project v72.** A model row may have `source: {path, sha256}` (`project/source_dto.rs`). A v71 file steps up unchanged and opens unlinked. A source on a row that is not a model, an empty path, a bad digest or an unknown key is a corrupt file. An older CamCraft refuses a v72 file by name (`unsupported project version 72`).
- **The check** (`crates/ui/src/model_link_watch.rs`). In the window, each linked file is checked about once a second; the frame timer comes back for it while a model is linked. A file is read again only when its size or time moved. A new digest imports the file again through `CommandKind::ImportFile`, and `finish_import` lands a linked file on its model by name. This is the existing re-import: one `UpdateModel`, one undo step, the operations go Stale. **Nothing regenerates or posts.**
- **An undo of that import stays.** The check does not import the same bytes again; only a new change imports.
- **A missing or unreadable file** keeps the model as it is and is said on the status line one time.
- **Unlink.** The Browser's model menu has "Unlink from <file>" (`CommandKind::UnlinkModel`, `SetModelSource`, one undo step). The MCP tool `set_model_link` links (to a path, its digest recorded now, no import) or unlinks (`null`). `get_job` shows `models[].source`.
- **SHA-256** is the kernel's FIPS 180-4 code, re-exported as `camcraft_geometry::solidcraft::sha256_hex` (native only). No new crate dependency.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/2463-linked-model.md`.

## Readings

Live app, debug build, macOS: `camcraft-ui --mcp-port 7921 bracket.stl` (a 40 x 20 x 10 box).

- Before: `get_job` gives `bracket`, bounds max (40, 20, 10), `source.sha256` `00ee0c922a5b…`.
- The file is written again as a 40 x 20 x 25 box. Seven seconds later: bounds max (40, 20, 25), `source.sha256` `0158db27604b…`. No refusal in the log.

## Pinning tests

`crates/app/tests/model_link.rs`:
- `an_import_from_a_file_links_the_model_to_that_file`
- `an_update_trades_the_link_and_undo_restores_it`
- `delete_and_undo_keep_the_link`
- `link_and_unlink_are_one_undo_step_each_and_refuse_by_name`
- `the_project_file_keeps_the_link_and_a_v71_file_opens_unlinked` (also: a v73 file is refused by name)
- `a_malformed_source_row_is_refused_as_corrupt`
- `the_mcp_tool_links_and_unlinks_and_get_job_shows_the_source`

`crates/ui/src/model_link_tests.rs`:
- `a_changed_file_is_imported_again_as_one_undo_step_and_its_operations_only_go_stale` (a generated Face operation goes Stale, no generation starts, undo restores it and stays)
- `a_missing_file_keeps_the_model_and_is_said_one_time`
- `unlink_stops_the_check_and_undo_links_again`

`cargo xtask gate quick` after merging upstream main (136f19763): 891 steps, 0 failed (ui lib suite: 1219 passed). Then upstream main 4dddc3872 was merged (one conflict: `examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.camproj`, kept at version 72; upstream had moved it to 71 in 80df80145): `continuous_4axis_part` (with its new `the_committed_project_uses_the_current_file_version`), `model_link` and `sketch_project` pass; clippy clean. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-geometry --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Changes to tests outside this feature

- `crates/app/tests/continuous_4axis_part.rs`: the test imports its model from a file, so the model is now linked and the saved example would carry this machine's absolute path. The test unlinks the model before it saves; the committed example names no file. `examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.camproj` is written again (`WRITE_GOLDEN=1`): only `"version"` changes (72).
- `crates/app/tests/sketch_project.rs`: `assert_eq!(PROJECT_VERSION, 71)` is now `const { assert!(PROJECT_VERSION >= 71) }`. The DXF profile row still arrives at v71; a later step does not break the test.

## Not exercised

- Windows and Linux: not run. The check uses std file metadata only.
- A window that the operating system reports as occluded does not draw frames (existing behaviour), so the check waits until the window is shown.
- A file renamed or moved away reads as missing; link it again with `set_model_link`. There is no "Link to file…" item in the window yet.

## Why

Solidcraft proposes "Send to CamCraft" (tangency-labs/solidcraft#18936, Solidcraft RFC 0001 phases 1 and 3). Each save in Solidcraft writes the `.sc` file again; with this, CamCraft updates the part after each save.

Process change: yes (`.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`: the `set_model_link` row).

Effort: high
Fork synced at v0.24.0 (upstream main 4dddc3872 merged in; the project version is 72, as #2441, #1517, #2016 and #1862 took 68 to 71).

**What changed**

- A `.mch` file can state `controller.post`, the name of a built-in post. `Machine.post`
  holds it. A file without the key reads as before.

- The validator also refuses a name that is not a built-in post, and a post that does not
  serve the machine's kind. The post crate gets the registry as a closure, as the holder
  lookup does (#828), so there is no new crate edge.
- `posting::post_offer` returns `Option<PostOffer>`. It offers the machine's named post

  the setup's post. Otherwise it gives the kind offer as before (`OfferWhy::Kind`). A

body:
## What changed

Add Do not touch selections for protected model faces and edge chains on 2D Offset and 3D Pocket. Clearance applies to the flute, shank, and holder. Generation refuses unsafe cuts, raises obstructed rapid links, and blocks NC posting when protection is violated.

The Geometry controls support undo and redo. The MCP tools use the same commands. Cached viewport overlays show protected selections and record frame cost.

`PROJECT_VERSION` advances from current main's v71 to v72. Readers that support v71 must refuse protected files before they can discard `do_not_touch`. Main's DXF fields and migration notes remain intact.

Latest review fixes:

- Pin the v72 format barrier and protection persistence. Migrate the historical example through load/save before strict comparison. Preserve the DXF introduction floor at v71. No fixture files changed.
- Resolve the inherited modal tool axis for each move.
- Bound the full assembly rotation between midpoint poses. The margin adds each interval's angular swing times the assembly reach, plus the arc deviation. Nonfinite bounds are refused.

## Validation

Head: `39e6c84e87cb22fcbc4499bd8630741a38024cc1`. Merged upstream main at `49501a9b9e57c15aa3b9f6f1ba9a6e8c3180ce05`.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: GREEN after a targeted rerun. The initial full run had 617 steps: 615 passed and two version-specific tests failed. After the two test updates and the constant assertion guard, `--failed` reran both failed steps on the final head with zero failures. `continuous_4axis_part` passed all 9 tests; `sketch_project` passed all 14 tests. The full 617 steps were not repeated on the final head.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: GREEN on the final head, 0 warnings and 0 errors (21.37 s).
- `do_not_touch_post_gate_blocks_violations_and_project_v72_persists`: 1 passed.
- Modal-axis regression: `omitted_axis_inherits_tilted_pose_for_protection` — passed in `verify_avoid` (5 passed).
- Rotating-assembly regression: `detects_protected_edge_contact_between_rotating_poses` — passed in `verify_avoid` (5 passed).
- Mutation checks: all three failed with the fix removed and passed after restoration.
  - Format 72 changed to 71: E0080 at the older-reader floor assertion. Restored 72: the persistence pin passed.
  - Reverted modal-axis resolution: the inherited path returned `[]` instead of `AvoidHit` at move 1, shank, 1 mm. Restored resolution: the pin passed.
  - Removed the swing bound: the rotation pin failed with `rotation must enclose contact between midpoint poses: []`. Restored the bound: the pin passed.

Earlier validation on `e11845b0c741207e747510d1f221f0dc47aa698f` passed the vertical-arc, constructor, and overlay-cache pins. These are previous results, not validation of this head.

## UI review evidence

Both images use the same 2200 × 1200 scene and camera. The after image shows the protected face and edge-chain rows, clearance, and viewport marks. Screenshots remain on the fork's images-only branch.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: parent Boundary UI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/37652ad68277c01babd8fb2996b41ed38e4cc7bd/2149/before.png) | ![After: protected rows, clearance, and viewport marks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/37652ad68277c01babd8fb2996b41ed38e4cc7bd/2149/after.png) |

The structural pin `geometry_boundaries_shows_do_not_touch_controls_rows_and_viewport_marks` checks the protected-item rows.

## Not exercised

The release gate, ignored heavy tests, snapshot comparisons, and manual interactive GUI checks were not run for this fix.

Process change: yes
Changelog: Add "Do not touch" protected faces and edges on 2D Offset and 3D Pocket (crates/app, crates/motion, crates/sim, crates/ui).
Fixes #2055

title: feat(ui): report door with prefilled GitHub issue and clipboard screenshot
body:
## What changed

The status strip gains a Report door next to the Debug info door (#1696).
It opens a small window:

- A short title field.
- Two buttons, "Report a bug" and "Request a feature". Each opens the
  browser on a prefilled GitHub new-issue URL: the title, the body and the
  `bug` / `enhancement` label are already typed.
- A "Copy screenshot" button. It asks the shell for a picture of the whole
  application window: egui's `ViewportCommand::Screenshot`, answered by the
  native shell's capture module (`shell_window/capture.rs`, a second render
  pass of the same frame into a private texture). The picture goes to the
  clipboard. The user pastes it into the issue description and GitHub
  uploads it.

The body embeds the Debug info report (#157), so both paths carry the same
fields from one source. When no answer arrives, the copy names that in
words, in the status line.

Provenance: the mechanism is egui's public capture contract. The maintainer
pointed at SolidCraft's report dialog for the shape only; their code was
not read and their look is not used.

The repository also gains `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/blank-issue.md` and
`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml` (GitHub reads `blank_issues_enabled`
only from that path). The new glyph `act-report.png` is the Tabler Icons
(MIT) `banner` glyph; its SVG master `assets/ui/svg/act-report.svg` sits
with our masters and `assets/ui/LICENSES.md` names Tabler as its source.

## How tested

- `report_tests.rs` (new, kittest): URL encoding; the prefilled URL shape;
  the body content; the door open and a kind button filing the URL; the
  typed title in the URL; a kind button asking the shell for the whole
  window; the answer copying the picture and saying the word; the copy
  after the window is closed; an answer for another token left alone; no
  answer copying nothing. 10 tests.
- `structural.rs`: the door sits on the status strip; no floating window is
  open by default (pin kept).
- `op_icon_table.rs`: the `Report` glyph is SVG-mastered and unique.
- `cargo xtask icons --check`: 0 breaches.
- The maintainer GUI-tested the debug build on 2026-11-17 and said it looks
  good: door, window, browser open with the prefilled issue, and the
  whole-window picture on the clipboard.
- Quick gate on the final head is named in the ready comment below.

## Not exercised here

- Clipboard paste into GitHub in an automated test: the tests assert the
  clipboard write, not GitHub. The maintainer's GUI test covered the paste
  path.

Note for the reviewer: this PR touches `.github/`, so `pr-test.yml` refuses
it and the review builds locally (read, not built: the yellow
`needs-maintainer` path).

Branch merges origin/main at 16658f67b.

Changelog: The status strip gained a Report door: it opens a prefilled GitHub issue and copies a whole-window screenshot to the clipboard (#1696, PR #1798)

Fixes #1696

title: feat(finish3d): gap_link - a straight link across gap openings
body:
Adds the finish3d `gap_link` parameter: a dropdown with `Jump` (default, today's retract/clearance hop, unchanged) and `Straight` (one straight Feed link between the run ends at their own tip height - no rise, no traverse, no plunge).

What changed:
- `camcraft_motion::finishing3d`: new `GapLink` enum (default `Jump`) and `Finish3DParams.gap_link`; new `gaplink.rs` with the `Straight` verdict; the `emit_runs` chain tries the straight link on a break the `ramp` diagonal refused, and keeps the plain hop when the verdict says no.
- The law: the line is fixed (both run ends are legal tangent centers by the march's own construction), so the exact segment-triangle sweep of the move at the budget `r - TOUCH_EPS` answers the whole question. Grazing rims pass, a real bite refuses, and a refusal takes the `Jump` hop byte for byte as every older file ran.
- Serpentine fix: a raster line broken by openings now runs back WHOLE (`pieces.reverse()` plus each piece's points). Reversing only the points made every gap link jump back across the whole field instead of crossing its gap. This shortens the existing `Jump` traverses on broken lines too.
- Project file: the words `jump` and `straight`, written always like `ramp` - no version step-up; older files read as `jump`. The digest takes tag `0x4D` plus a variant byte only when the choice is not `Jump`, so ops that hop as before keep their old stamp.
- UI: "Gap link" combo (Jump / Straight) in the Mill 3D passes section. MCP: the same words ride the existing `edit_operation` params door and undo.

How tested: `crates/motion/tests/finish3d_gaplink.rs` - 6 pins: the jump pin (byte-for-byte old behavior), straight links over a holed plate at the run height, every straight link kept clear of the facets (exact sweep scan, Prime Directive), straight refused over a biting slot keeps the plain hop (byte-for-byte `Jump` crossings), and every hop traverse spans one gap, never the field (fails on the pre-fix serpentine with a 31.7 mm field jump). Round-trip pins in `crates/app/tests/project_roundtrip.rs` (jump/straight/absent) and the params-door test in `crates/app/tests/mcp.rs`. Quick gate on the touched crates green; the finish3d release verdict lanes and `golden_cl` / `operations` / `project_roundtrip` / mcp / ui structural suites green.

Not exercised: geodesic ring chains (keep the plain hop, unchanged); patterns other than the march rasters.

GUI check: the maintainer approved the two-option surface (`Jump` as before, `Straight` as here) in chat after testing the Straight link over the holes in his 171 mm STEP part on an intermediate build; the `Straight` law itself is unchanged in this rebuild. A release build of this head is available for a re-test.

Changelog: finish3d gap_link: a straight link across gap openings (Jump / Straight) (#1708, PR #1713)

Base note: the head branch is on the tbrasselle/Camcraft fork (the gh account has no write access on this repo); it branches from this repo's main at 101d82f9, so it merges clean.

Fixes #1708
